item.title: Pentagon Inspector General Declines to Investigate Starlink Service Disruptions in Ukraine
item.description: A bipartisan group of nine U.S. senators, comprising four Republicans and five Democrats, has been denied a request to investigate the throttling of Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine. The Defense Department's inspector general (IG) declined the lawmakers' inquiry, stating that the Air Force is better equipped to address concerns regarding the slowdown. The senators sought the probe after Ukrainian officials reported that connection speeds on both Starlink and its military-grade counterpart, Starshield, had been reduced, hampering Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian drones. A congressional aide, speaking anonymously, characterized the IG's decision as a refusal to examine Musk and Starlink's role, despite the office's capability to do so. The aide noted that congressional concerns about Musk's control over Starlink have persisted for years, contributing to the development of Starshield. item.title: 1960 Aloha Week Parade in Honolulu Captured in Vibrant Kodachrome Photos
item.description: The 1960 Aloha Week Parade in Honolulu, Hawaii, is vividly captured through a series of vintage Kodachrome photographs, offering a nostalgic glimpse into mid-century Hawaiian culture and traditions. Established in 1946 to celebrate Hawaiian heritage, Aloha Week featured a vibrant array of cultural elements including colorful floral floats, pāʻū riders in traditional attire, marching bands, and the Royal Court parading through Waikiki's streets. The Kodachrome film's rich, saturated colors beautifully preserved the tropical flowers, bright costumes, and festive atmosphere of the event, providing a detailed visual record of the parade's pageantry. Among the images are specific scenes such as a Chinese-themed float with members of a Lion Dance organization, the Bridge of Friendship, Civic Club displays, debutantes from Kaimuki JCC, and the King and Queen of Aloha Week, Henry Rosa and Barbara Kukaua. item.title: Stripe Billing Coordination Design Prevents Duplicate Payment Attempts
item.description: Stripe Billing has a built-in feature called Smart Retries that automatically handles failed subscription payments by retrying at optimal times based on network and issuer signals. However, when merchants add a recovery layer on top of Stripe's system, a coordination problem arises: two systems may attempt to retry the same failed payment, leading to duplicated attempts, wasted resources, and potential double-charging. The Swipe Again team, which provides a recovery solution for Stripe Billing merchants, has developed a coordination design that integrates with Stripe's native retry system rather than competing with it. Their approach reads Stripe's current state before each retry decision, using observable invoice data such as attempt_count, next_payment_attempt, and decline codes. The system defers attempts if Stripe is about to retry within 24 hours, fires into gaps in Stripe's schedule, and only runs full recovery plans when Stripe has exhausted its retry attempts. item.description: Ellis Boyle, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina, made controversial remarks during a conservative livestream on October 21, suggesting that removing the 'worst 5 percent of the population' from society and preventing them from having children could significantly reduce crime within a few generations. Boyle cited a claim that '5 percent of the population cause 90 percent of the crime,' a statistic he said he encountered before verifying it. item.description: Michael Gleason, husband of Amy Gleason, who served as acting administrator of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), began working as a senior adviser in the Health and Human Services Department's Office of the Assistant Secretary for Planning and Evaluation in May 2025. His appointment came just 33 days after significant layoffs at the Health and Human Services Department (HHS), which had been heavily impacted by DOGE-driven cuts. The division, responsible for health policy research and analysis, had recently undergone substantial staff reductions, making Gleason's hiring notable. item.description: Savannah Chrisley, the 29-year-old reality TV star, has publicly defended her relationship with her fiancé Jason Galanis, 56, following her announcement of pregnancy and engagement. In a recent episode of her 'Unlocked' podcast, Chrisley addressed the significant age difference between her and Galanis, acknowledging it as 'huge' but emphasizing that it does not affect her happiness or commitment to their relationship. item.description: According to leading political analysts, four Republican incumbents may have significantly impacted their party's chances of maintaining control of the House of Representatives. The Cook Political Report, a nonpartisan ratings group, has quietly adjusted the rankings of four Republican lawmakers' races from 'toss up' to 'leaning Democrat' just weeks before the November 3 election. This change reduces the number of toss-up races from 21 to 17, lowering the Republicans' prospects of retaining House control. Democrats now hold 186 solid districts, 18 likely districts, and 16 leaning districts, totaling 220 seats if Cook's predictions hold true. item.description: Lisa Guerrero, a former ABC 'Monday Night Football' sideline reporter, expressed shock and hurt after Michele Tafoya, a Republican Senate nominee backed by Donald Trump, dismissed her miscarriage on a 2023 podcast. Tafoya, who had worked alongside Guerrero on the same sports broadcast team, questioned the severity of Guerrero's miscarriage and labeled her a 'drama queen' during the podcast episode. Guerrero had kept her miscarriage private due to feelings of trauma and humiliation, and Tafoya never contacted her directly, according to the Washington Post. Tafoya's podcast episode disputed Guerrero's account, claiming she had experienced multiple miscarriages herself and suggesting Guerrero sought attention. item.description: A hacking group known as the Department of Peace infiltrated an internal Department of Homeland Security (DHS) database, revealing personal information of approximately 42,000 employees, including agents from Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP). item.description: The pro-MAGA podcast 'The Charlie Kirk Show' descended into chaos during a segment where former Republican strategist Tim Miller challenged the hosts' claims about President Donald Trump's record. item.description: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and 20 states have filed a lawsuit against Dollar General, alleging deceptive pricing practices that have overcharged consumers for years. The complaint states that Dollar General repeatedly mislabeled prices, failed to correct discrepancies despite knowing about the issue, and extracted millions of dollars in unlawful overcharges from vulnerable shoppers. The lawsuit, filed on September 11 in U.S. District Court, argues that the federal government has supremacy over state regulations under the Constitution's supremacy clause. item.title: FDA scientists oppose Health Secretary Kennedy's push to allow unapproved peptide drugs
item.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has encountered significant resistance from Food and Drug Administration (FDA) scientists regarding his efforts to expand access to injectable peptide drugs. According to an Associated Press report, six sources familiar with the policy development revealed that most FDA scientific staff opposed the initiative, expressing concerns that it could undermine the agency's mission to prevent unproven health products from entering the U.S. market. Kennedy's Department of Health and Human Services initially sought a regulation that would classify certain peptides as safe for use by compounding pharmacies, which create customized medications. However, FDA officials warned that scientific staff had substantial safety concerns and would not endorse a regulation declaring these substances safe. item.title: LaKeith Stanfield and Ben Wheatley Replace Rob Savage in 'Molepeople' Horror Film
item.description: Paramount Primal and Blumhouse Atomic Monster have announced significant changes to their upcoming horror film 'Molepeople.' LaKeith Stanfield, who was previously announced as a star, has exited the project, and director Rob Savage has departed due to scheduling conflicts. Ben Wheatley, known for his work on films like 'Normal' and 'Kill List,' will now take over as director. The film, which was unveiled during Blumhouse Atomic Monster's New York Comic-Con presentation earlier this month, follows a man who descends into the abandoned tunnels beneath New York City and discovers a 'twisted society' living there. Written by Nathan Elston, 'Molepeople' is co-financed and co-produced by Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Paramount Primal, with Paramount handling worldwide distribution. The film is scheduled for a theatrical release on August 27, 2027. Producers include Jason Blum, J.D. Lifshitz, Raphael Margules, and James Harris. Savage will remain as an executive producer alongside Ryan Turek,

item.title: Trump demands removal of Democratic candidate from Alaska Senate race, accuses Democrats of election fraud
item.description: President Donald Trump has issued a series of aggressive statements on his Truth Social platform, accusing Democratic officials in Alaska of election fraud and demanding the removal of Senate candidate Mary Peltola from the ballot. Trump's claims stem from a New York Times investigation that linked Peltola's campaign and national Democratic operatives to efforts to recruit a candidate named Dan Sullivan for the Alaska Senate race. Trump alleged that Democrats 'illegally searched for, and recruited' Dan Sullivan to run against Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, claiming this was an attempt to 'defraud, confuse, and obfuscate the Election.' He further accused Peltola's campaign of making 'false statements under oath in Federal Court,' which he labeled as perjury, and demanded that she face 'very serious consequences.' item.title: Ramaswamy's attack ad backfires in Ohio governor race, GOP fears internal fallout
item.description: According to an internal GOP poll obtained by Axios, Republicans are concerned that Vivek Ramaswamy's attack ad is harming his bid for governor of Ohio. The survey, commissioned by a Republican group, shows Democrat Amy Acton leading by eight points, up from a two-point lead she had before the ad began circulating on October 19. The poll, conducted among 800 likely voters from October 23 to 26, found Acton's support rising from 47 percent to 50 percent, while Ramaswamy's support dropped from 45 percent to 42 percent. Eighty-six percent of respondents were aware of the ad, and those who knew about it were twice as likely to favor Acton, according to a memo. A separate Suffolk University poll also indicated a four-point gap, narrower than the nine-point lead shown in late September. The ad features Acton's estranged mother, Donna Arthur, accusing her daughter of lying about her childhood. item.title: MS NOW Host Clarifies Trump's Legal Status During Ohio Governor's Race Discussion
item.description: During a segment on the Ohio governor's race, MS NOW host Alicia Menendez intervened to correct a guest who referred to President Donald Trump as a 'convicted sex offender.' The discussion initially focused on Democratic Senate candidate Sherrod Brown criticizing a campaign ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother, who lost custody after refusing to protect her from sexual assault by her stepfather. Brown expressed hope that Republican Senator Jon Husted would pressure Vivek Ramaswamy to withdraw the ad, but noted Husted instead aligned with Governor Mike DeWine, Trump, and JD Vance in defending it. Guest Richard Stengel then claimed Trump 'gets a pass' for conduct that would disqualify other politicians, stating he was a 'convicted sex offender' and suffering from 'frontal lobe dementia' without providing evidence. item.title: Nanotyrannus Skeleton Fetches $47.3 Million at New York Auction, Sparking Scientific Debate
item.description: The mounted skeleton of a newly identified dinosaur, nicknamed Jodi, has sold at auction for $47.3 million, making it the second-most valuable dinosaur fossil ever sold. The 10-foot-tall skeleton, initially mistaken for a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex, was confirmed by researchers to belong to a distinct genus, Nanotyrannus, in October 2023. The auction, conducted by Sotheby's in New York, saw intense bidding among six parties over a 12-minute period. The sale has reignited discussions within the scientific community about the ethics of private fossil sales versus public display. Sotheby's described Jodi as an 'excellent exhibition-ready' skeleton with 191 fossil elements and a nearly complete skull, noting it is one of only three such skeletons known to science. The skeleton was discovered in Montana's Hell Creek Formation by rancher Jodi Pierson and later excavated by commercial paleontologist Clayton Phipps, who also discovered the famous 'Dueling Dinosaurs' fossil. item.title: Trump faces potential new Espionage Act charges as DOJ strategy in Comey case could impact future cases
item.description: The Justice Department is laying the groundwork for potential new Espionage Act charges against former President Donald Trump by filing a criminal information in a case against former FBI Director James Comey, according to legal experts. The filing, made on October 5, 2026, just before the 10-year deadline for Espionage Act prosecutions expired, aims to establish a legal precedent that could help prosecutors bypass the need for a grand jury in future cases involving Trump. The case against Comey, which prosecutors argue meets the 10-year deadline set by Congress, has drawn attention because it could set a precedent for how the Justice Department handles charges related to Trump's alleged mishandling of classified documents at Mar-a-Lago. Comey's lawyers have challenged the filing, arguing that it allows the government to keep allegations 'hanging over' a defendant indefinitely without a grand jury indictment. item.title: Julia Roberts' Early Breakthrough Role in 'Mystic Pizza' (1988) Revealed
item.description: The filming of Mystic Pizza in the fall of 1987 marked a pivotal moment in Julia Roberts' career, propelling her to fame just two years before she became a global superstar. At 19, Roberts was relatively unknown, having been cast as the fiery, rebellious Daisy Araújo despite not being the first choice. Director Donald Petrie chose her for her infectious laugh and raw talent, which allowed her to hold her own alongside more seasoned actors. Roberts described Daisy as 'full of fire and full of spice,' and the role provided her with a creative 'free-for-all' that let her act without restraint. Her co-stars later recalled that Roberts was the most fun on set, thanks to her energetic and happy nature. The movie, set in Mystic, Connecticut, was filmed in a replica set built in a warehouse and a converted home in Stonington, as the real Mystic Pizza was too small for filming. item.title: Federal Judge Blocks Trump Administration's Use of Taxpayer Funds for Campaign Ads
item.description: U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan has issued a ruling blocking the Trump administration from using $20 million in taxpayer funds for television advertisements promoting President Trump. The judge criticized the administration's unfulfilled promise to stop using public money for the ads, noting that the advertisements continued to air with the 'Paid for by the U.S. Government' disclosure for at least another week after Trump's October 5 pledge. The ruling follows a separate court order in New York that had already blocked the taxpayer-funded advertisements through mid-November, well beyond the November 3, 2026, elections. Judge AliKhan concluded that officials likely used public dollars to unlawfully finance a national campaign in the final weeks before the November 2026 elections. The judge expressed skepticism about the administration's assurances that the same issue would not recur, stating that the sequence of events gave the court reason to doubt these promises. item.title: Border Security Official Uses Former Secretary's Luxury Jet Amid Feud
item.description: Border Security Official Tom Homan, a vocal critic of former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, has reportedly been using a luxury Gulfstream jet that was previously associated with Noem, according to a Substack newsletter called The PunchUp. The jet, a $53 million Gulfstream G650 with tail number N472US, flew from Washington's Reagan National Airport to San Juan, Puerto Rico, last Tuesday and then to West Palm Beach the following day. This usage comes amid a bitter feud between Homan and Noem, who was fired as Homeland Security Secretary in March 2026 following a series of controversies, including her use of a $200 million Gulfstream G700 fleet and a leased Boeing 737 with luxury amenities. The feud intensified after two American citizens were killed during an immigration crackdown in Minneapolis, leading to Trump appointing Homan to oversee the operation as a rebuke to Noem. item.title: FDA streamlines gene therapy approvals, Missouri AG targets Lilly's 340B data demands
item.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has published draft guidance aimed at streamlining approvals for individualized gene therapies, a move welcomed by rare disease advocates who have long criticized the agency's previous approach. Under the current system, companies must submit separate drug approval applications for each patient's customized gene therapy, even when using fundamentally the same method to target different genes. This process has been deemed prohibitively expensive by advocates, who argue it creates unnecessary regulatory burdens. The new draft guidance formalizes a 'plausible mechanism pathway,' offering clearer rules for licensing and updating gene editing treatments. Separately, Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway has sent a cease-and-desist letter to Eli Lilly, demanding the company stop requiring hospitals to provide claims data to receive discounted medicines under the federal 340B Drug Pricing Program. item.title: Saab introduces Sea Giraffe AMB D radar with 155-mile air detection range and anti-jamming capabilities
item.description: Saab, the Swedish defense company, has unveiled its latest naval radar system, the Sea Giraffe AMB D, designed to detect and track air and surface threats at extended ranges. The radar boasts a 155-mile (250-kilometer) detection range for air targets and 31 miles (50 kilometers) for surface targets. Built on the Sea Giraffe AMB family, the new system integrates active electronically scanned array (AESA) technology with a software-defined architecture, enabling rapid beam steering and multi-tasking capabilities. This allows the radar to monitor multiple areas simultaneously while providing timely threat information. The system incorporates electronic counter-countermeasures (ECCM) to resist jamming attempts by adversaries, a critical feature in modern electronic warfare environments. Saab emphasizes the radar's modular design, which supports integration with other naval systems and allows for continuous software upgrades without requiring hardware replacement. item.title: Mississippi Democrat Scott Colom says Trump's rally visit shows GOP anxiety as race tightens
item.description: Mississippi Democratic Senate nominee Scott Colom has responded to President Donald Trump's recent rally in his state, calling it a sign of Republican anxiety and using the event to bolster his fundraising efforts. In a fundraising email sent Wednesday, Colom detailed how Trump's Monday rally at Crossroads Arena in Corinth targeted him and his campaign, accusing the former president of spreading 'hate and lies' about him. Trump attended the event to support Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-Miss.), whom Colom is challenging in a Senate race that has become unexpectedly competitive in a traditionally Republican state. Colom stated, 'I think we're under their skin,' suggesting that the Republican Party's heightened focus on his campaign indicates they are feeling threatened. He noted that Trump's presence in Mississippi was specifically to ensure Hyde-Smith's victory, but added that polls show the race is a statistical tie with his campaign gaining momentum. item.title: Susan Saint James: Early Career and Iconic 1960s Television Roles
item.description: Emmy-winning actress Susan Saint James passed away on October 26, 2026, at the age of 80 after battling pancreatic cancer. While she gained widespread recognition in the 1970s and 1980s through roles in 'McMillan & Wife' and 'Kate & Allie,' her career began to take shape in the mid-to-late 1960s. At age 20, she landed her first major television role in the pilot film 'Fame Is the Name of the Game,' portraying Peggy Maxwell, a sharp editorial research assistant. The pilot was developed into a full series called 'The Name of the Game' in 1968, where she continued her role. Her performance earned her three Emmy nominations and a win for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Drama Series in 1969. Saint James distinguished herself in an era of traditional Hollywood glamour by embracing a relatable 'girl next door' persona rather than high-fashion modeling looks. item.title: Disney Bus Driver Shares Journey from Church Minister to Theme Park Employment at 51
item.description: Michael Bowen, a 51-year-old bus driver at Walt Disney World, shares his career transition from a church minister to working at Disney. After years in religious ministry, Bowen felt unfulfilled and sought a change. In 2017, during a vacation to Florida, he realized he could pursue a career as a Disney bus driver. He moved to Florida in 2020 at age 44, after obtaining a Florida driver's license, and began working as a bus driver for Disney. He appreciated the stable job with benefits like health insurance, paid time off, and retirement plans, which were unavailable in his previous church positions. In 2022, Bowen left Disney following a difficult divorce, moving to Oregon where he drove city buses but remained unhappy. He later met his current wife through his Disney-focused YouTube channel, 'Incognito Mouse,' and returned to Disney in 2026 at age 50. item.title: Right-Wing Activist James O'Keefe Charged with Unlawful Voting in Minnesota Polling Place Stunt
item.description: Conservative provocateur James O'Keefe, founder of O'Keefe Media Group, has been criminally charged with identity theft and unlawful voting following a polling place stunt in Minneapolis during Minnesota's primary election. The incident, which was captured in videos posted online in August, involved members of O'Keefe's group, dubbed the 'Justice League,' attempting to test Minnesota's voter vouching system. During the stunt, one group member dressed in a burqa and another used an accent while posing as a voter named 'William Pomeranz,' a real Minneapolis registered voter. The group claimed they were merely asking election workers about the vouching process, not impersonating anyone. However, Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced criminal charges against O'Keefe and Cam Higby, alleging identity theft and unlawful voting. item.title: MAGA Rally Speakers Avoid Trump References as Crowd Energy Falters
item.description: The article examines recent MAGA rallies held in October 2026, noting that speakers at these events rarely mentioned Donald Trump, a stark contrast to previous years. The author, an anthropologist who has studied Trump and the MAGA movement for years, attended rallies in Pennsylvania, Michigan, and Mississippi, observing a noticeable decline in crowd enthusiasm compared to 2024 events. Poll data from mid-October 2026 supports this observation, showing only one-third of U.S. adults approve of Trump's job performance, with 71% believing the country is on the wrong track. item.title: Trump's Political Calculations Risk Military Safety in Iran War Timing
item.description: The article criticizes former President Donald Trump for publicly disclosing that the U.S. is delaying a major military offensive against Iran until after the upcoming election. The author argues that Trump's admission, made during a press briefing, unnecessarily reveals the political vulnerability of the military operation to Iran, potentially giving the Iranian government time to prepare countermeasures. The piece emphasizes that Trump's decision to share this information with the media, rather than providing a more strategic explanation, puts U.S. troops at greater risk by making the military's position transparent to adversaries. The article notes that Trump's statement contradicts the usual practice of keeping military strategies confidential, especially when they involve potential conflicts with foreign powers. item.title: Joe Rogan's Growing Criticism of Trump's Policies Raises Concerns for Republican Midterm Prospects
item.description:
Joe Rogan, the popular podcaster known for his significant influence on political discourse, has shifted from his previous endorsement of Donald Trump to expressing growing criticism of the president's policies, particularly regarding foreign affairs and domestic governance. According to a Bloomberg report cited in the article, Rogan has become increasingly vocal about Trump's second term, criticizing broken promises and the ongoing conflict with Iran. 'What Trump stood for, some of it turned out to not be real,' Rogan stated during a recent conversation with actor Michael Douglas, adding that the president's promise of 'no wars' was contradicted by the current military engagement with Iran, which he described as 'a giant quagmire.'

item.title: Mary Trump warns of Trump administration's efforts to undermine midterm election integrity
item.description: Mary Trump, the niece of former President Donald Trump, has issued a stark warning about her uncle's alleged plan to manipulate the upcoming midterm elections. In her Substack newsletter titled 'SCAM: Donald's Plan to Rig the Midterms,' she describes the situation as a 'five alarm fire' and emphasizes that this election represents the most critical in modern history. item.title: Vance's donor network under scrutiny in Brazil corruption probe
item.description: Vice President JD Vance has become the center of a Brazilian police investigation regarding whether his co-founded donor network, the Rockbridge Network, illegally supported Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign. Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered the investigation following Bolsonaro's loss in the October 25 runoff election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The investigation focuses on whether Rockbridge, which Vance co-founded in 2019, provided foreign financial assistance to Bolsonaro's campaign, which is illegal under Brazilian law. Dino's 38-page order directs federal police to examine communications between Rockbridge representatives and Brazilian businessmen Tallis Gomes and Pedro Sang, who are alleged to have facilitated financial support for Bolsonaro's campaign. item.title: CBS's '60 Minutes' struggles with declining ratings amid revamped format
item.description: CBS's '60 Minutes' has experienced a significant ratings decline in its latest episode, drawing only 5.64 million total viewers and 558,000 viewers in the 25-54 demographic, according to Nielsen figures obtained by Status' Oliver Darcy. This performance marks a notable drop from historical averages, as the sixth episode of a '60 Minutes' season has not drawn fewer than 7 million total viewers or 1 million in the key demographic since 2000. The show, which underwent a major overhaul under CBS News chief Bari Weiss, is now facing criticism for failing to improve its performance, with 'America's Funniest Home Videos' and 'The Price Is Right' outperforming it in the crucial 25-54 demographic. A veteran TV executive noted that the show's previous hosts, such as Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega, were well-regarded, and the current direction has reportedly made the show 'worse' in the eyes of viewers. item.title: Fox News viewership declines amid shifting political interests
item.description: Fox News is experiencing a significant drop in viewership, with October 2026 marking the network's lowest-rated month since December 2023, according to media newsletter Status. The decline is particularly pronounced among the 25-54 age demographic, which advertisers prioritize, with Fox News averaging just 98,000 viewers in this group—a 32% drop from the previous year. This represents the lowest-rated month for this demographic in 25 years. While Fox News still leads cable news overall, beating ESPN in total day viewership despite the return of football, the ratings decline is notable given the political context of the upcoming 2026 midterms. Weekday prime time shows hosted by Sean Hannity and Laura Ingraham are also seeing their lowest-rated months in both total viewers and the 25-54 demo since December 2023. item.title: Supreme Court Conservatives Push to Overturn Landmark Religious Freedom Ruling
item.description: The Supreme Court's conservative majority appears poised to potentially overturn a landmark 1990 ruling that has shaped religious freedom cases for decades. According to a CNN analysis cited in the article, the Court may deliver a significant victory for religious conservatives by revisiting Employment Division v. Smith, a decision written by the late Justice Antonin Scalia. The case in question, St. Mary Parish v. Roy, involves Catholic preschools and the Archdiocese of Denver seeking to participate in Colorado's universal preschool program without signing the state's nondiscrimination agreement covering sexual orientation and gender identity. A federal appeals court had previously ruled in favor of Colorado, relying on the Smith precedent which holds that neutral laws applicable to all do not require a 'compelling interest' to justify them. item.title: Jennifer Lopez Announces New Single 'Proof of Love' Amidst Vinyl Reissue of 2011 Album 'Love?'
item.description: Jennifer Lopez is preparing to release her new single 'Proof of Love,' which will serve as a bonus track on the first-ever vinyl edition of her 2011 album 'Love?,' set for release in November. The singer revealed that the song was inspired by the emotional transition her life underwent when her twins, Max and Emme Muniz, left for college. Lopez described the song as a 'happy dance song' that also addresses 'pain and grief when someone's gone,' emphasizing that the song aims to transform grief into a positive marker of love. She shared that the experience of her children leaving home prompted her to return to the studio, resulting in what she considers some of her best work to date. The 'Love?' vinyl reissue, which includes three different versions available for pre-order starting October 28, coincides with the premiere of her new concert film 'The JLo Show: Live in Vegas,' airing on CBS and Paramount+ on Thanksgiving night, November 26. item.description: The Washington Post reports on a new three-part Netflix documentary featuring Matthew Perry, the late 'Friends' star, which delves into his personal life and career struggles. The documentary, titled 'Matthew Perry: The Documentary,' includes interviews with Perry's close friends and family members who share intimate details about his battles with substance abuse throughout his adult life. The film begins with archival footage of Perry in his early 20s, struggling financially while waiting for his breakthrough role as Chandler Bing on 'Friends.' In one of the old interviews featured in the documentary, Perry reflects on his early days, saying, 'I haven't prayed often, but I made a prayer and I said, God, you can do anything you want to me, just please make me famous.' The documentary provides a candid look at Perry's journey from his early career to his later years, highlighting both his professional successes and personal challenges. item.title: Trump's Louisiana Data Center Payment Claim Debunked by Local News Investigation
item.description: President Donald Trump made a false claim during a recent interview, stating that every resident living near a Louisiana data center received a $10,000 check. The claim was debunked by WWL-TV, a local New Orleans news station, which investigated the matter and found no evidence of such payments. Trump's statement was made during an interview with Fox2 Detroit's Roop Raj, where he referenced a community in Louisiana that supposedly received $10,000 payments, leading to widespread support for the data center project. However, Louisiana Economic Development, the state agency responsible for economic development projects, confirmed they were unaware of any direct payments to residents. Spokesperson Emma Wagner stated, 'If there were $10,000 payments, I'd be shouting it from the rooftops.' item.title: Historian Mark Bray returns to U.S. after fleeing death threats, releases book on antifa targeting
item.description: Mark Bray, a historian and Rutgers University professor, has returned to the United States after being forced to flee with his family due to death threats and doxxing by far-right activists. The threats intensified after Bray's book 'Antifa: The Antifascist Handbook' was targeted by conservative groups, particularly Turning Point USA, which pushed for his dismissal. Bray's new book, 'Unpunctuated Death Threats,' set for release in January, details his experience of being labeled as part of a terrorist organization despite antifa being a decentralized movement against fascism, white supremacy, and racism. Bray criticized the right's narrative that portrays antifa as a top-down, organized entity funded by George Soros, calling it a recurring tactic that dates back to the Occupy Wall Street era. item.description: A former Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) staffer, Farijah 'Doc' St. Clair, has issued a stark warning to Americans about an impending crisis, urging immediate preparation. St. Clair, who now leads technology and intelligence at Crisis24, a risk firm owned by GardaWorld, shared his concerns on social media platform X, stating that 'your window to prepare, even with the basics, is closing.' St. Clair cited European governments advising citizens to stockpile supplies and Pentagon directives requiring U.S. military bases to sustain operations for 90 days as significant indicators of the severity of the situation. item.title: SoFi Technologies Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Performance with $1.4 Billion in Revenue and $241 Million Net Income
item.description: SoFi Technologies, Inc. (SOFI) has reported its third quarter 2026 financial results, showcasing a record net revenue of $1.4 billion and net income of $241 million. The company's performance reflects significant growth across multiple business segments, with fee-based revenue reaching $1.429 billion for the quarter, up from $1.101 billion in the same period of 2025. Key drivers of this growth include strong performance in loan origination fees, technology services, and the newly launched SoFi Crypto platform. The company's loan origination fees increased to $607.6 million in Q3 2026 compared to $327.8 million in Q3 2025, while technology services revenue rose to $263.6 million from $151.7 million. The SoFi Crypto platform, launched in Q4 2025, contributed $3.7 million in net crypto transaction revenue during the quarter. SoFi's regulatory capital metrics also demonstrated strength, with CET1 risk-based capital at $9.52 billion, representing a 16.9% ratio against risk-weighted assets.

item.description: Democrats in Washington state have successfully turned the Republican strategy against them regarding a ballot measure targeting transgender athletes. The proposed measure, which would require students to obtain health care provider verification of their sex to participate in girls' sports, has been countered by Democrats who frame it as government overreach rather than focusing on transgender athletes. This approach has united the party's progressive and moderate wings, with figures like Rep. Pramila Jayapal and Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez both opposing the measure. Jayapal emphasized using conservative values against them by highlighting the intrusion of government into family decisions. item.title: GOP Consultant Identifies 'Red Scream' as Key Threat to Senate Majority in Upcoming Midterms
item.description: A veteran Republican consultant, Alex Castellanos, has introduced the term 'Red Scream' to describe growing frustration among conservatives and independents who feel ignored by Donald Trump and Republican leaders ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. According to an Axios report cited in the article, this frustration could lead to lower voter turnout among these groups, potentially costing Republicans control of the Senate. Senate Republicans are currently assessing their prospects in several key states, with Iowa appearing to favor them, Ohio showing signs of slipping, and Alaska and Kansas viewed with increasing pessimism. item.description: Democrats are capitalizing on reported fractures within President Donald Trump's 'Make America Healthy Again' (MAHA) coalition, which has been a key component of his political base. The coalition, initially formed around promises to improve food safety and reduce harmful chemicals in the food supply, has faced internal disputes over the pace of policy changes, particularly regarding pesticide regulations. item.title: TikTok Creators Monetize Copper Wire Stripping as a Side Hustle Amid Rising Prices
item.description: Copper prices have reached record highs, driving a surge in TikTok content where creators demonstrate stripping copper wire for resale. The trend, which has gained traction among diverse users including hobbyists, electricians, and teenagers, involves documenting the process of removing insulation from copper wire to sell the metal. According to the article, copper prices hit $14,473 per metric ton in September 2026, more than double the 2020 price, making scrap copper highly valuable. While some creators earn modest income from selling stripped copper, many generate significant revenue through TikTok Shop by promoting wire strippers and other tools. For example, one creator reported earning $1,446 from a video with 6.8 million views, while another sold over 20,000 wire strippers globally. item.title: The Institute of Housing and the Skin of Madrid: A Historical Reflection on Urban Development
item.description: The article discusses the historical context of housing policies in Spain, particularly under the Franco regime, and their lasting impact on urban development. It references the Instituto Nacional de la Vivienda (National Housing Institute) and its role in shaping residential areas, especially in Madrid. The author, Juan Manuel Grijalvo, explores how housing projects during Franco's era were designed to create a sense of stability and control, often displacing rural populations into urban outskirts. The text includes personal anecdotes from readers about living in neighborhoods built during this period, such as Colmenar Viejo, which were initially seen as undesirable but later became valuable due to their location. The discussion also touches on the political implications of housing policies, comparing the current state of public housing in areas governed by different political parties, such as PSOE and PP. item.title: GOP Claims Hidden Advantage in Senate Races Amid Democratic Missteps
item.description: The National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) has been promoting a 'hidden advantage' for Republicans in the 2026 Senate races, claiming Democrats have made a 'huge mistake' by focusing too much on Texas while neglecting other traditionally Democratic states. In a fundraising email sent to donors, the NRSC criticized 'the Democrat media' for publishing polls showing Republican losses in Texas and accused outlets of 'gushing' over Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico's fundraising success. The email asserted that Republicans are 'SURGING in historically blue states!' and cited Minnesota as an example, claiming that Senate nominee Michele Tafoya is 'statistically TIED' with her Democratic opponent, though no specific poll was referenced. item.title: U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency Confirms China's Reusable Spaceplane in Satellite Image
item.description: The U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) has confirmed that a satellite image circulating since 2024 depicts China's secretive reusable orbital spaceplane, resolving earlier uncertainty about its identity. The image, originally captured by Maxar Technologies (now Vantor), was first publicly shown in 2024 by U.S. Space Force Col. John Patrick during the Open Space Forum in South Korea. The DIA's 2026 report, 'Challenges to Security in Space 2026,' includes a higher-resolution version of the photograph, providing one of the clearest public views of China's experimental spacecraft. The report explicitly identifies the object as a Chinese spaceplane, noting its similarities to the American X-37B, an uncrewed reusable orbital vehicle operated by the U.S. Space Force. item.title: Egyptian court orders closure of independent news outlet Mada Masr and fines editor-in-chief
item.description: An Egyptian court has ordered the closure of Mada Masr, one of Egypt's last remaining independent news outlets, and imposed a fine of three million Egyptian pounds ($53,400) on its editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, for operating an unlicensed website. The New Cairo Misdemeanour Court also ordered the confiscation of the outlet's equipment and devices. Attalah was taken into custody following the ruling but was released hours later after Mada Masr paid the full fine. During her release procedures, Attalah learned she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to one year in prison on charges of publishing false news and running an unlicensed website. Mada Masr's editorial criticized the court's actions, stating it entered court 'with a measure of faith in the law and the justice system' but found 'none of that faith intact.' item.title: Trump Banishes Bill Maher After Dinner Criticism, Echoes Soup Nazi Analogy
item.description: The article discusses a recent incident involving former U.S. President Donald Trump and comedian Bill Maher following a White House dinner. After Maher criticized Trump's low midterm approval ratings and mocked his behavior on his HBO show, Trump responded with a 1,300-word Truth Social post banning Maher from future dinners. The piece draws parallels between Trump's behavior and the 'Soup Nazi' character from Seinfeld, emphasizing Trump's demand for absolute loyalty at his dinners. item.title: 1940s Brussels Street Life Captured in Vintage Photographs
item.description: The article presents a collection of 30 vintage photographs capturing everyday street life in Brussels during the 1940s. These images document pedestrians, shoppers, workers, and residents navigating the city's streets and squares throughout a decade marked by World War II occupation and postwar recovery. The photographs include specific locations such as Boulevard Adolphe Max and Boulevard Anspach, with dates ranging from March 1941 to October 1947. The images provide a historical record of urban life during the German occupation period (1940-1944) and the subsequent post-liberation era (1945-1947). The photographs show the subdued atmosphere of wartime Brussels alongside the renewed energy of the postwar period, offering a nostalgic glimpse into the city's daily movements and urban landscape more than eighty years ago. item.title: Women Athletes Face Higher Risk of Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (RED-S) with Subtle Early Symptoms
item.description: The article discusses Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (RED-S), a condition that occurs when athletes do not consume enough calories to meet the demands of their training or basic physiological needs. Women are at significantly higher risk than men, with a 2026 study in the Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport finding that 70% of high-level female athletes were at risk of developing RED-S. The condition can lead to a range of symptoms including fatigue, impaired concentration, frequent illnesses, poor recovery, irregular periods, weakened immune systems, and increased risk of injuries such as stress fractures. Early signs include persistent fatigue, longer recovery times after workouts, declining performance, more frequent illnesses, poor sleep, increased hunger, mood swings, hair loss, and weight loss. More serious symptoms include irregular or absent periods and frequent injuries. The article emphasizes that RED-S is not just about undereating but reflects chronic underfueling

item.title: Jio Platforms' stock surges 21% in debut following record-breaking Indian IPO
item.description: Jio Platforms, the Indian telecom and digital services unit owned by billionaire Mukesh Ambani and backed by Meta and Google, experienced a 21% surge in its stock price during its market debut on Wednesday. The company raised $3.2 billion through India's largest and most subscribed initial public offering (IPO), which attracted over $77 billion in investor bids. The shares opened at ₹1,358 (approximately $14) per share, up from the IPO price of ₹1,119 ($12), valuing Jio Platforms at around ₹12.5 trillion ($131.9 billion). This makes it India's second-most valuable listed company after its parent Reliance Industries, which is valued at approximately ₹16 trillion ($168.6 billion). The IPO, which ran from October 21 to 22, saw bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer, with over 13.8 million applications, marking a record for the most subscribed stock offering in India. item.description: The Dallas Cowboys secured a crucial 38-21 road victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, ending a two-game losing streak and keeping pace with the 4-2-1 New York Giants in the NFC East. Quarterback Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes, including two to CeeDee Lamb and one to George Pickens, while running back Javonte Williams rushed for a career-high 155 yards, scoring the game-sealing touchdown with 2:21 remaining. The Cowboys' offense, which had struggled in recent games with only 29 combined points in their last two outings, showed significant improvement, marking the first time since 1983 that they achieved over 200 yards rushing and passing in a single game against the Eagles. item.title: Thunderbird: A Concept Space Station Designed Without Traditional Floors
item.description: The Thunderbird expandable space station, designed by OMI (Of My Imagination) in collaboration with Florida-based startup Max Space, represents a groundbreaking approach to space station architecture. Unlike traditional space stations that rely on gravity-defined floors, Thunderbird's interior design eliminates the concept of 'up' and 'down,' creating a circular layout where every surface can function as a floor. The station, which can be launched on a single SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, unfolds in orbit to approximately twenty times its folded size, providing 350 cubic meters of pressurized space—roughly a third of the International Space Station's volume. Its soft architecture, composed of layered fabric including Kevlar, meets or exceeds NASA safety standards for heat, vacuum, vibration, and micrometeoroid impacts. item.description: A federal judge has ruled that Bill Essayli, Los Angeles' top federal prosecutor, is unlawfully serving in his position and has barred him from overseeing two criminal cases. Senior U.S. District Judge J. Michael Seabright determined that the Justice Department had unlawfully delegated powers to Essayli, effectively making him a 'de facto' United States Attorney without proper Senate confirmation. The judge's ruling rejects the Justice Department's attempt to maintain Essayli's authority through a revised delegation of powers, stating that the revised arrangement made no meaningful difference as the powers in question could not have been lawfully delegated to him. Essayli, a former Republican California Assembly member, has been a key legal enforcer for the Trump administration, pursuing charges against protesters and activists while dropping cases involving administration allies. item.description: Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel has encouraged hecklers to continue shouting a specific phrase at President Donald Trump during his rallies. item.description: The article explores the growing 'sovereign baby' movement, where parents reject traditional medical systems and government documentation for their children. It highlights the deep distrust of medical institutions, particularly among women of color, who face systemic disparities in maternal care. item.description: Pokémon Unite, the free-to-play MOBA game developed by Tencent Games and published by The Pokémon Company, is set to end its service on the Nintendo Switch in March 2027. This announcement has been met with mixed reactions from the gaming community, with many players expressing disappointment over the game's monetization practices and the lack of alternatives for console players. item.title: Chiricahua Becomes America's 64th National Park, Celebrating Unique Geological Formations
item.description: Chiricahua National Monument in southeastern Arizona has been officially designated as America's 64th national park, marking the first new addition to the national park system in six years. Located in the Chiricahua Mountains, the park features a unique landscape of balanced rocks and rhyolite spires that have formed over millions of years. The area, known to the Apache people as 'the land of standing-up rocks,' covers approximately 12,000 acres of canyon country and includes hundreds of pinnacles that can reach up to hundreds of feet in height. The geological formations were created by volcanic activity approximately 27 million years ago, when the Turkey Creek eruption deposited vast amounts of ash that later cooled and fractured into columns. Over time, water erosion and freeze-thaw cycles shaped these columns into the distinctive spires seen today. item.title: Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Calls for International Attention on Kashmir, Resource Management, and Energy Infrastructure
item.description: Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain Azar addressed the Karachi Press Club during a Meet the Press event, emphasizing the need for greater international focus on the region's constitutional status, natural resources, and economic challenges. He expressed concerns about the proposal to grant Gilgit-Baltistan provisional provincial status, stressing that the region's constitutional and political issues must be resolved before any such move. Azar criticized India's 2019 decision to revoke Jammu and Kashmir's special status, arguing that the international community has failed to take meaningful action against Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. item.title: Elsa Lanchester's Early Career in 1920s London: Cabaret, Film, and Stage
item.description: Elsa Lanchester, the British actress later famous for her role as the Bride of Frankenstein, began her career in the late 1920s in London's vibrant bohemian scene. Before achieving Hollywood fame, she established herself as a multifaceted performer through cabaret ownership, music hall comedy, and early film roles. In the early 1920s, she co-founded and managed The Cave of Harmony, a popular London nightclub that became a hub for avant-garde artists and intellectuals including Evelyn Waugh, Christopher Isherwood, and Osbert Sitwell. Lanchester gained recognition for her satirical performances, often wearing top hats, tights, and high heels while performing cheeky, socially critical sketches and singing Victorian-era ballads. Her recordings, such as 'Please Sell No More Drink to My Father' (1926), were released on Columbia Records. item.title: Earwax's Dual Properties Offer Insights for Developing Natural Insect Repellents
item.description: Earwax, medically known as cerumen, has long been recognized for its role in ear health, but recent research reveals its unique physical properties could inspire safer insect repellents. Scientists from Georgia Institute of Technology conducted experiments observing how ants interact with earwax, discovering it possesses a paradoxical combination of slipperiness and stickiness. The study, published in the journal Soft Matter, found that earwax's structure—composed of skin flakes held together by a binder—creates a surface that ants struggle to navigate. When ants attempted to climb smooth earwax, they immediately fell due to the material's ability to absorb the moisture from their wet suction cups, preventing attachment. This dual property, known as shear-thinning, allows earwax to thin under physical deformation while maintaining its sticky nature. item.title: SK Hynix predicts memory shortages will continue through 2030 amid AI-driven demand
item.description: SK Hynix, a leading South Korean memory manufacturer, has forecasted that global memory shortages will persist until at least 2030, driven by surging demand from artificial intelligence infrastructure development. SK Hynix attributes this success to a 'virtuous cycle' where AI adoption drives increased infrastructure investment, which in turn fuels further AI development. The company noted that supply is not keeping pace with market growth due to technical challenges in leading-edge manufacturing processes and lengthy facility construction timelines. item.title: Religious and racial divides shape Brazil's presidential election dynamics
item.description: Brazil's 2026 presidential election revealed deep political divisions rooted in religious and racial identities, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva securing a narrow victory over Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. According to the article, 57% of Brazilians identify as Catholic and 27% as evangelical, reflecting a significant shift from three decades ago when 80% were Catholic. Evangelicals, who form a growing political force with nearly one-fifth of Brazil's Congress identifying as such, largely supported Flávio Bolsonaro, while Catholics tended to back Lula. item.description: The Los Angeles city attorney's office has filed a lawsuit against Wagmor Pets, an animal rescue organization once popular among Hollywood celebrities, alleging it operates as an illegal commercial enterprise. The lawsuit claims owner Melissa Bacelar purchased dogs from puppy mills and resold them to adopters at high prices, charging up to $1,500 per dog while falsely portraying them as rescued animals. item.title: Los Angeles Board Suspends Utility Shutoffs Amid Unusually High Bills
item.description: The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (DWP) board has suspended residential water and electricity service shutoffs for nonpayment through the end of the year following a period of unusually high utility bills. The board, which does not have the authority to forgive the charges, encouraged residents to enroll in programs that could help alleviate rising costs. The move comes as complaints about unexpectedly high bills have spread widely on social media, with residents describing bills as 'outrageous,' 'insane,' and 'extremely crazy.' item.description: Right-wing podcaster Candace Owens has expressed satisfaction over a recent court decision that removed her personally from a defamation lawsuit filed by French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife, Brigitte Macron. item.description: Thousands of voters in North Carolina, a key battleground state for the 2026 midterms, are encountering significant issues with their mail-in ballots due to a new Republican-imposed requirement that the inner ballot envelope must be completely sealed inside the outer envelope. According to data compiled by Common Cause North Carolina from statewide election data through October 24, 2026, nearly 6 percent of mail ballots counted so far have been flagged with problems, totaling 3,672 ballots still in jeopardy. item.description: The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed an appeal with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit following a federal judge's decision to block President Donald Trump's plans for renovating East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, D.C. item.title: Apple releases iOS 27.2 update featuring expanded Siri AI language support and security enhancements
item.description: Apple has released iOS 27.2 for iPhones and iPads, introducing expanded language support for Siri AI in French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish, with the ability to remember details from past conversations. The update also includes improved memory functions for Siri, allowing it to tap into sources like photos in Messages, calendar events, voicemails, Safari history, and reading lists. Carter expressed strong skepticism toward the Trump administration's Justice Department during a court hearing regarding an emergency request to halt California from counting mail ballots from over 20,000 registered voters. item.title: Twitch Streamer Hasan Piker Sues Commentator Scott Jennings Over Defamatory Claim
item.description: Hasan Piker, a Twitch streamer and leftist commentator, has filed a defamation lawsuit against Scott Jennings, a pro-MAGA pundit, in a Washington, D.C. federal court, seeking over $72 million in damages. The complaint, reported by Bloomberg Law, alleges that Jennings aired an altered clip and fabricated quote on his podcast in August, falsely claiming Piker had called for lynching Black Americans. Piker states the clip was a 42-second heavily edited segment from a 2024 Twitch stream where he was sarcastically mocking another person's criminal justice argument, not expressing his own views. item.description: The 1953 Chevrolet Corvette marked the beginning of one of the most iconic American sports cars. Every 1953 Corvette was finished in Polo White with a red interior and powered by a 150-horsepower "Blue Flame" inline-six engine paired exclusively with a two-speed Powerglide automatic transmission. Featuring a groundbreaking fiberglass body, the car combined sleek European-inspired styling with American engineering. Though production was modest and performance modest by later standards, the 1953 model established the Corvette name and laid the foundation for decades of legendary sports cars to follow. item.title: Satellite data confirms AMOC weakening trend over 30 years
item.description: Satellite measurements have provided some of the strongest evidence yet that the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC), a crucial ocean current system that transports warm water from the Gulf of Mexico to the North Atlantic, is weakening. According to research published in New Scientist, the AMOC has slowed by 14 percent over a 30-year period, based on analysis of heat flux from the ocean to the atmosphere. The study, led by Richard Allan of the University of Reading, UK, used satellite data to measure how much heat the North Atlantic is releasing into the atmosphere, finding an 18 percent decrease in heat flux over 40 years. This decline in heat release correlates with the AMOC's reduced ability to transport warm water northward, which helps maintain Europe's relatively mild climate. item.title: Medieval Bookmarks: Practical Tools for Manuscript Readers
item.description: The article explores the history and variety of medieval bookmarks, which were practical tools used by readers to mark their place in manuscripts. Unlike modern decorative bookmarks, medieval bookmarks were functional and often made from available materials. The author, Jenneka Janzen, identifies three main types of medieval bookmarks: fore-edge bookmarks, register bookmarks, and found object bookmarks. Fore-edge bookmarks consisted of tabs made from parchment, leather, or woven beads, stitched or looped into the page at the desired text location. These were commonly found in liturgical books, helping readers locate specific readings during religious services. Register bookmarks resembled modern bookmarks and came in three variations: simple strips attached to the book's endband, portable versions with strings attached to an anchor, and a sophisticated rotating dial system that indicated column positions in multi-column texts. item.description: Nanette Fabray (October 27, 1920 – February 22, 2018) was an American actress, singer, and dancer who reached the peak of her mainstream fame during the 1950s. Transitioning seamlessly from Broadway to television and film, Fabray became a household name through her work on 'Caesar's Hour' (1954–1957), where she served as Sid Caesar's main comedic partner. Her exceptional sketch comedy timing and musical talents earned her three Emmy Awards during her tenure on the show. She unexpectedly left the series in 1956 due to a contractual misunderstanding between her business manager and Caesar, a conflict that took years to resolve. Fabray also starred in the critically acclaimed musical film 'The Band Wagon' (1953), where she played Lily Marton, a character inspired by Broadway legend Betty Comden. item.title: Chinese Scientists Uncover 'D-rex,' a Fungus Evolving Since Dinosaur Extinction
item.description: Chinese scientists have identified a new species of fungus, Dianjunus rex, which they've nicknamed 'D-rex,' that represents the largest known ascomycete fruiting body. The fungus, discovered in Yunnan Province, China, can grow up to 50 cm (20 inches) tall and weigh nearly 5 pounds, significantly larger than previous records. Its evolutionary lineage dates back approximately 65 million years, coinciding with the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event that wiped out non-avian dinosaurs. Researchers from the Kunming Institute of Botany established that this fungus belongs to a new family, Dianjunaceae, within the order Xylariales. The discovery challenges previous assumptions about fungal size limits and suggests that environmental changes following the dinosaur extinction may have facilitated its evolution. Raw Story's Editor-in-Chief, Adam Nichols, explained that the company believes every American deserves access to reliable, independent journalism to understand what's happening and what's at stake. item.title: Russian Realist Painter Abram Arkhipov Captures Peasant Life in Vibrant Early 20th-Century Art
item.description: Abram Efimovich Arkhipov (1862-1930), a Russian realist painter born into a rural family in the Ryazan region, is celebrated for his vivid portrayals of peasant life in early 20th-century Russia. After studying at the Moscow School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture and briefly at the Imperial Academy of Arts, Arkhipov became a member of the Wanderers and later the Union of Russian Artists. His early works featured somber, realistic scenes of hard labor, particularly focusing on women's experiences in rural settings. Over time, his style evolved to embrace brighter colors and more luminous compositions, capturing peasant women in traditional attire against sunlit backgrounds. These later works, characterized by their rich hues and radiant quality, remain among the most distinctive representations of rural Russian life from the period. item.title: Exercise Reshapes Heart's Nerve Control System Differently on Left and Right Sides
item.description: Regular exercise does more than strengthen the heart; it physically reshapes the nerves controlling heart function, according to new research from the University of Bristol. Published in Autonomic Neuroscience, the study reveals that moderate aerobic exercise changes the structure of nerve cells in the stellate ganglia, which regulate heart activity. Surprisingly, these changes differ significantly between the left and right sides of the body. In trained rats, the right-side nerve cluster contained about four times as many neurons as the left, while neurons on the left nearly doubled in size and those on the right became slightly smaller. The findings suggest that exercise produces side-specific structural changes in the heart's nervous control system, potentially offering new insights for treating heart conditions like arrhythmias, angina, and stress-induced 'broken-heart' syndrome. item.title: Personalized mRNA Vaccine Shows 42% Reduction in Melanoma Recurrence Risk in Phase 3 Trial
item.description: A new personalized mRNA vaccine developed by Merck and Moderna has demonstrated significant efficacy in reducing the risk of melanoma recurrence, according to Phase 3 clinical trial results. The vaccine, called Intismeran Autogene, was tested in combination with Pembrolizumab, an immunotherapy drug, and showed a 42% reduction in the risk of cancer recurrence or death compared to Pembrolizumab alone. The INTerpath-001 trial included 1,137 high-risk melanoma patients who had undergone complete tumor removal surgery. Participants were divided into two groups: one receiving Pembrolizumab alone and the other receiving Pembrolizumab combined with the mRNA vaccine. After an average follow-up of 24.6 months, 82.2% of patients in the combination therapy group remained recurrence-free, compared to 70% in the Pembrolizumab-only group. item.title: Charles Montaigne: Dutch Designer Who Shaped Parisian Haute Couture in the Mid-20th Century
item.description: Charles Montaigne (1900–1989), born Martinus Meuwese in Tilburg, Netherlands, was a prominent Parisian couturier who achieved significant recognition in French haute couture. Montaigne was known for his refined, elegant designs that catered to a sophisticated clientele, maintaining an active presence through the 1950s and 1960s. His influence extended beyond his own work; he founded a couture school in Amsterdam that later evolved into the Amsterdam Fashion Institute. item.title: Coffee Grounds Converted to Biochar Enhance Concrete Strength by 30 Percent
item.description: Scientists from RMIT University in Australia have discovered that coffee grounds, a significant source of organic waste, can be transformed into biochar through a process called pyrolysis, which significantly enhances the strength of concrete. Each year, approximately 10 billion kilograms of coffee waste is generated globally, much of which ends up in landfills, contributing to environmental issues such as greenhouse gas emissions. The research team, led by engineers Rajeev Roychand and Jie Li, found that heating coffee grounds to over 350°C in an oxygen-deprived environment produces a porous, carbon-rich biochar that can bond with cement, increasing concrete strength by up to 30 percent. This innovative approach addresses two major environmental challenges: reducing landfill waste and decreasing the demand for sand, which is often extracted from riverbeds through environmentally damaging mining practices. item.description: California is poised to make history with Proposition 40, a groundbreaking measure that would impose a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires residing in the state as of January 1, 2026. The tax, if approved, would generate approximately $100 billion over five years, with 90% allocated to healthcare and 10% to education, food assistance, and tax administration. This initiative represents a significant step in what economist Gabriel Zucman describes as 'the battle of the 21st century'—a movement to tax extreme wealth that has gained momentum across the United States. The proposal has drawn strong opposition from billionaire donors, including Google co-founder Sergey Brin, who has contributed $100 million to campaigns against the measure. Despite concerns about potential billionaire exodus and economic impacts, proponents argue that wealth creation is inherently collective and that billionaires have benefited disproportionately from public infrastructure and services. item.title: Early Years of the Bee Gees: Rare Photos from Their 1960s Rise
item.description: The Bee Gees, before becoming the iconic disco-era band known for their falsetto harmonies and white suits, were a successful baroque pop and psychedelic rock band in the 1960s. Originating from Australia, the Gibb brothers—Barry, Robin, and Maurice—began performing as teenagers in the late 1950s and early 1960s. They made their first national TV appearance on August 12, 1960, with a song written by 13-year-old Barry Gibb. Influenced by the Beatles and the British beat movement, they started recording professionally in 1963. Their breakthrough came with the Australian number-one hit 'Spicks and Specks' in late 1966, after which they moved to London to pursue an international career. In 1967, they signed with manager Robert Stigwood and released their international debut single 'New York Mining Disaster 1941,' which was initially mistaken for a Beatles recording due to its melodic harmonies. item.title: Noel Clarke Denies Six Sexual Offense Charges in London Court
item.description: British actor, writer, and director Noel Clarke appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court in London and pleaded not guilty to six sexual offense charges. The 50-year-old faces two counts of sexual assault, three counts of voyeurism, and one count of exposure. The allegations involve five women and are said to have occurred between 2007 and 2016. Clarke entered not guilty pleas to all six charges during the hearing, confirming only his name, date of birth, and address. The charges followed a year-long investigation by London's Metropolitan Police. The Crown Prosecution Service authorized the prosecution after reviewing a file of evidence. Clarke is known for playing Mickey Smith in 'Doctor Who' and for writing and appearing in the 'Kidulthood,' 'Adulthood,' and 'Brotherhood' films. He also co-wrote the Sky drama 'Bulletproof' with Ashley Walters. The court granted Clarke bail, and he is scheduled to appear next at Southwark Crown Court on November 18. item.title: Gardaí Seek Public Help to Identify Unidentified Man Found Dead at Dublin Recycling Facility
item.description: Gardaí have released a description and photograph of a tracksuit top worn by an unidentified man whose body was discovered at a waste recycling facility in Clondalkin, Dublin, on October 24th. The man, described as aged between 20-50 years, slim build, white complexion, brown/blonde hair, and without tattoos, had been at the facility for several days before being found. Workers at the recycling depot discovered the body just before 1 a.m., immediately halting operations and alerting An Garda Síochána. The scene was secured pending a pathologist's examination, after which the remains were transported for a postmortem. Gardaí have committed homicide investigation resources to the case, with a senior officer leading the inquiry and an incident room established at Ronanstown Garda station. The discovery follows a pattern of human remains found in recycling or refuse mounds at processing depots, including the case of Andrew Haire, a 35-year-old from Co Meath found in July at the same facili

item.title: Ultra Right Beer Company Faces Backlash as Customers Wait for Unfulfilled Orders
item.description: The story details the situation of customers who ordered Ultra Right Beer, a brand marketed as a 'woke-free' alternative to Bud Light, but have not received their products. Seth Weathers, a MAGA political consultant, launched Ultra Right Beer in 2023 after a right-wing backlash against Bud Light for featuring transgender actress Dylan Mulvaney in a promotional campaign. Weathers marketed the beer through his 'Conservative Dad' persona, claiming it was '100 percent woke-free.' Despite initial success with over $1 million in sales claims and media attention from Fox News, the company failed to deliver products to customers. The Better Business Bureau gave Ultra Right Beer LLC an 'F' rating due to nearly 200 complaints about unfulfilled orders and poor customer service. Many customers, including a New Jersey police officer and an Oregon transportation employee, have reported never receiving their beer, with some orders taking over a year to arrive. item.title: IAEA Director Rafael Grossi Forecasts Tripling of Nuclear Power by 2060
item.description: Rafael Grossi, Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), has expressed optimism about the future growth of nuclear energy, stating that global nuclear power usage could more than triple by 2060. Speaking during the IAEA's annual report to the United Nations General Assembly, Grossi highlighted that this expansion will be driven by increasing electrification needs, the rise of AI-powered data centers, and technology companies seeking reliable, carbon-free energy sources. He emphasized that nuclear energy is increasingly viewed by nations as a key component of energy security, positioning it alongside solar power as a viable and safer alternative to other energy options. Grossi's remarks come amid growing global interest in nuclear power as a stable, low-carbon energy source, with several countries actively pursuing nuclear energy projects to meet climate goals and enhance energy independence. item.title: Trump Considers Expanding Pardon Scope to Include Junior White House Staff
item.description: President Donald Trump is reportedly considering expanding his preemptive pardon program to include junior staffers within his administration, according to The Washington Sun. The move would extend protection beyond senior officials who designed policies to those implementing them, particularly in contentious areas like immigration, military actions, and trade. This development follows Senator Elissa Slotkin's (D-Michigan) remarks urging accountability for 'the people who enabled' corruption within the Trump administration, which sparked conservative backlash and doxing campaigns against her staff. Slotkin argued that young professionals should be deterred from participating in government roles that could lead to legal issues, stating, 'I want young people coming out of school ... to be like: Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don't want, and so let me avoid participating in that.' item.title: Elon Musk Repeats Historical Inaccuracy About Hitler Being a Socialist
item.description:
Elon Musk has been criticized once more for repeating the false claim that Adolf Hitler was a 'socialist,' specifically labeling him a 'far left socialist.' This is not the first time Musk has made this error; in January, he responded to a Twitter user by stating that Hitler was a 'far left socialist' because his party was called the National Socialists. In August, he tweeted about the 'inescapable logic' that 'Hitler was a far-left socialist' and 'therefore, socialists are Hitler.' Recently, Musk shared a video from another account, adding, 'Hitler was a far left socialist. Literally in the name of his party!'
Historians and critics have repeatedly debunked this claim. Melanie D'Arrigo of the Campaign for New York Health clarified that Hitler was a 'far-Right fascist' whose party, the National Socialist German Workers' Party, was named to attract working-class voters. item.title: Jang Nara Returns as Divorce Lawyer CEO in 'Good Partner 2' Season
item.description: The drama 'Good Partner 2' has revealed new details about Jang Nara's role as Cha Eun Kyung, a divorce lawyer who has become the managing attorney of REBOM, a law firm she built from scratch. In the upcoming season, Cha Eun Kyung is depicted as a successful CEO with 50 employees, having earned recognition as one of the 'Women of the Year.' Jang Nara, who reprises her role after a two-year hiatus, shared insights about her character's evolution, emphasizing that the new season focuses on deeper empathy for clients as Cha Eun Kyung navigates her role as a business leader. She noted that the character has moved away from the intense pressure and ambition of the first season, adopting a more relaxed approach to her work. The drama will premiere on November 20 at 9:50 p.m. KST, continuing the story of Cha Eun Kyung and Kang Hye Sung, an experienced divorce lawyer. item.title: Meta Suspends Muse Sharing Feature After Security Flaw Exposes User Conversations
item.description: Meta has suspended the sharing feature for its AI assistant Muse following a security flaw that allowed researchers to easily access sensitive user conversations shared via web links. The flaw, discovered by security firm Claroc, enabled enumeration of 6,800 share links created by users, with researchers accessing hundreds of these links to find confidential information including executive search notes, internal revenue reviews, loan applications, bank fraud alerts, real estate performance reports, and staff vacation calendars. The vulnerability stemmed from Muse's URL structure, which included conversation titles in the subdomain (e.g., home-sale-budget-9f21c8a3.cf.metaaiusercontent.com), making links easily discoverable through passive DNS searches. Meta had marketed Muse as 'built from the ground up for privacy and security,' but the flaw contradicted this claim. item.title: Samay Raina Penalizes Contestant for Marriage Remarks on India's Got Latent, MC Stan Awards Zero
item.description: On the popular Indian comedy show 'India's Got Latent,' host Samay Raina gave a contestant a minus 10 score after the contestant, Rahul Bhatt, made comments about marriage and relationships that took an unexpected turn. During the show, Bhatt performed a puppet show with his brother on the dhol, and when asked about his marriage, he expressed that he found marriage more difficult than having an affair, stating that in a marriage, one cannot easily break up and get back together as they can in an extramarital relationship. He explained that ending a marriage could result in losing half of one's property, unlike affairs where relationships can be terminated and resumed. When directly questioned about whether he had ever cheated on his wife, Bhatt denied it, emphasizing that he was still married with two children and that he was happy with his wife. He highlighted that his wife took care of their children and family, making him happy. The panel, which included rapper MC Stan, comedian Tan

item.title: PHP developer Ondřej Surý plays critical role in global cybersecurity update
item.description: Ondřej Surý, a PHP developer working primarily in his spare time, has emerged as a key figure in maintaining internet security through his maintenance of PHP software packages for popular Linux distributions like Debian and Ubuntu. For over two decades, Surý has voluntarily kept these systems updated with the latest PHP versions, which power a significant portion of the world's websites. This week, when two major cybersecurity vulnerabilities were discovered in PHP, Surý quickly converted the necessary security fixes into easily installable packages for website operators. "The feeling is like I am responsible for all these people and I can't fail them," he told BBC News. Surý, who works full-time as director of DNS engineering at Internet Systems Consortium, explained that he received over $10,000 in donations within days - a year's worth of contributions he typically receives.
