item.title: Miss Manners Advises Against Insulting Telemarketers After Hanging Up
item.description: Miss Manners, a well-known advice columnist, addresses a reader's concern about whether it is appropriate to hang up on telemarketers without insulting them. The letter writer expressed regret for not insulting a telemarketer before ending the call, noting that telemarketers have adopted a new tactic of speaking continuously without allowing the recipient to interject or respond. The columnist emphasizes that while it is acceptable to end the call without engaging, it is not appropriate to resort to insults. Miss Manners explains that maintaining decorum, even in frustrating situations, is part of good manners. She argues that hanging up is a polite way to disengage from unwanted calls, but adding insults undermines the purpose of being courteous. The advice column highlights the importance of preserving social etiquette in everyday interactions, even when faced with persistent or annoying callers. item.title: Lula secures second term in Brazil, preventing regional rightward political trend
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has secured a historic second term in office, defeating Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in a pivotal election that has significant implications for Latin America's political landscape. The election, held on October 25, 2026, marked a decisive moment as Lula's victory halted what had been a noticeable trend toward right-wing governance across the region. Lula, who previously served as president from 2003 to 2010, made a remarkable political comeback after facing legal challenges and a period of political isolation. His victory over Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, represents a significant shift in Brazilian politics and has broader regional significance. The election results have been widely interpreted as a rejection of the right-wing policies that have gained traction in several Latin American countries in recent years. item.title: Texas Overcomes Ole Miss in Thrilling 34-27 Victory, Focuses on Ground Game and Special Teams
item.description: The Texas Longhorns secured a 34-27 victory over the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels on October 25, 2026, ending a losing streak and advancing their College Football Playoff hopes. The game featured a back-and-forth battle, with Texas building an early lead but struggling to maintain it as Ole Miss mounted a comeback. Key moments included Arch Manning's inconsistent performance, a critical interception, and a pivotal second-half drive that shifted momentum. Texas' ground game, led by Raleek Brown and Michael Terry, proved decisive in the second half, with an 80-yard drive culminating in a touchdown by Manning. The Longhorns also faced significant challenges on special teams, including a fake punt by Ole Miss that led to a crucial first down and a last-second onside kick recovery that was mishandled. item.title: Mid-Century Motel and Hotel Bedrooms Captured in Vintage Postcards from the 1950s and 1960s
item.description: The article explores the interior design of American motel and hotel bedrooms from the 1950s and 1960s, as depicted in vintage postcards. During this era, motels and hotels offered travelers accommodations that reflected the evolving design trends of the time. These spaces ranged from simple roadside stops with minimal furnishings to more stylish interiors featuring colorful bedspreads, patterned curtains, modern furniture, and contemporary amenities. Mid-century design principles influenced these rooms, emphasizing clean lines, practical layouts, and uncluttered aesthetics. Furniture often included simple wooden finishes, streamlined shapes, and tapered legs, with built-in headboards and compact bedside tables maximizing space efficiency. Color played a significant role in room design, with pastel shades like pink, mint green, and pale blue commonly used alongside warmer tones such as gold, brown, and rust. item.title: Elections Expert Warns of DOJ Lawsuit Over Alaska Ballot Confusion
item.description: An elections expert has raised concerns about the Trump administration's Justice Department (DOJ) filing a lawsuit against Alaska's midterm election certification. The DOJ claims voters might be confused by two candidates named Dan Sullivan on the ballot, arguing the state should not certify the election until an investigation into potential voter confusion is completed. This lawsuit comes months after Alaska's Supreme Court had already ruled that both Sullivans could remain on the ballot without issue. Marc Elias, a voting rights attorney and host of the 'Democracy Watch' podcast, criticized the DOJ's legal arguments as baseless. He pointed out that the law cited by the DOJ pertains to voter registration, not election certification, and questioned the administration's strategy in pursuing this case. item.title: Belarus Advises Citizens to Avoid Travel to Six European Countries Amid European Unrest
item.description: Belarus has issued a travel advisory urging its citizens to avoid non-essential travel to six European countries: France, Belgium, Italy, Spain, Portugal, and Albania. The advisory, released on Sunday, October 25, 2026, comes amid escalating protests and riots across several European nations. The Belarusian Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that political situations in these countries have deteriorated sharply, with potential for curfews and emergency measures that could disrupt public transportation, internet access, and communication networks. The ministry also warned that consular and legal assistance might be limited due to the small number of Belarusian diplomatic staff in these countries. For Belarusian citizens currently in the affected nations, the advisory recommends heightened vigilance, avoiding large crowds and protest areas, and monitoring updates from local authorities and Belarusian diplomatic missions. item.title: Juan Manuel Grijalvo Discusses Housing Policy and Communist Theory in Historical Context
item.description: The article features a response by Juan Manuel Grijalvo to reader comments regarding housing policy and political systems. Grijalvo addresses a comment that argues the longevity of the Franco regime (40 years) compared to the Soviet Union's 74 years demonstrates the success of communist systems. He counters that duration alone doesn't indicate a system's success, citing the Catholic Church's long history as an example. The author discusses the role of the Instituto Nacional de la Vivienda (INVI) during Franco's regime, noting that while there was some state intervention in housing, the economy remained largely controlled by oligopolistic business families. Grijalvo critiques the current autonomous state system in Spain, arguing it has created artificial competition between regions and is plagued by corruption, but suggests federalism as a potential solution. item.title: UK to equip RAF Chinooks and A400M aircraft for wildfire response
item.description: The UK government has announced plans to equip Royal Air Force Chinook helicopters and A400M Atlas aircraft with specialist firefighting equipment, creating a domestically based aerial wildfire-fighting capability for the first time. The aircraft will be available, when requested, to support civilian fire and rescue services battling blazes in difficult terrain such as remote moorland, steep hillsides, and other areas that are hard for ground crews to reach. Civilian services across all four UK nations will continue to request military assistance through the Military Aid to the Civil Authorities process. The announcement came at the UK’s first Wildfire Resilience Summit, held after a summer marked by unusually intense and sustained wildfires and extreme heat. Officials framed the move as part of broader preparation for future weather events driven by climate change. item.title: Former Trump aide warns of potential presidential exit amid Ukraine war discussions
item.description: A former Trump administration press secretary, Anthony Scaramucci, has predicted that President Donald Trump could be asked to leave office following the 2026 midterm elections if he proceeds with diplomatic talks involving Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping regarding the Ukraine conflict. Speaking on 'The Daily Beast Podcast' with host Joanna Coles, Scaramucci stated that such a meeting would be catastrophic for the Republican Party, declaring it would effectively 'kill' the party. He emphasized that Democrats do not need to win the Senate for this scenario to become plausible, noting that a 50-50 split in the Senate would require only 17 Republican senators to defect to force Trump's removal. Scaramucci expressed that many Republicans 'hate his guts' due to Trump's policies, including strikes against Iran and a deal to purchase Russian oil, which have alienated the party base. item.title: Trump Administration Advocates for Viktor Orbán as UN Secretary-General, Sparking Outrage
item.description: The Trump administration has reportedly been advocating for former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, a close ally of Russian President Vladimir Putin, to become the next United Nations Secretary-General. According to a Wall Street Journal report citing sources familiar with the matter, the administration is pushing for Orbán's potential candidacy despite his reservations about a nationalist politician holding such a high international position. Orbán has not officially declared his candidacy, but the report has sparked significant criticism from political analysts and media outlets. The Wall Street Journal's conservative editorial board criticized the idea, stating it would 'lift the veil by giving the U.N. a leader as low as Turtle Bay has already sunk.' Political analysts on social media, including Jim Stewartson, described the move as 'deliberate chaos,' comparing it to a 'bad frat party' where people 'start breaking stuff and throwing furniture.' item.title: Early 1900s Halloween Costumes: A Glimpse into Vintage Celebrations
item.description: The article presents a collection of 45 vintage photographs capturing Halloween celebrations in the early 1900s. These images showcase individuals of all ages—men, women, and children—wearing homemade and early commercial costumes. The costumes range from traditional figures like witches, ghosts, and skeletons to more imaginative disguises such as clowns, animals, and other character portrayals. The photographs offer a nostalgic look at how Halloween was celebrated before the holiday became heavily commercialized. The article emphasizes the simpler, more personal nature of these early celebrations, contrasting them with modern Halloween traditions. The collection is part of the Vintage Everyday blog, which focuses on historical imagery and cultural moments from the past. The blog's content is presented in a straightforward manner, without additional commentary or analysis beyond the visual documentation. item.title: Luka Dončić Scores 52 Points in Lakers' Victory Over Jazz
item.description: Luka Dončić delivered a standout performance for the Los Angeles Lakers, scoring 52 points and dishing out 10 assists in a 132-123 victory over the Utah Jazz on Sunday. The game saw Dončić dominate with a double-double, hitting eight three-pointers and showcasing his scoring prowess. The Lakers' offense was led by Dončić, with Austin Reaves contributing 29 points, while the Jazz struggled to contain the Lakers' star. Lauri Markkanen led the Jazz with 28 points, but the team's overall performance was hampered by a slow start from rookie Darryn Peterson, who shot 4-of-13 from the field. The Jazz also had contributions from Jaren Jackson Jr. with 20 points and Ace Bailey with 17 points and 12 rebounds. Despite the loss, the Jazz showed potential with Keyonte George's 24 points and 9 rebounds. item.title: Trump DOJ lawyers face skepticism from judges in California ballot dispute
item.description: Lawyers from President Donald Trump's Justice Department faced significant skepticism from judges during a court hearing regarding California's ballot counting procedures for the upcoming midterm elections. The hearing, held before the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals, centered on the DOJ's argument that California must set aside ballots cast by noncitizen voters. The three-judge panel, including two judges appointed by Trump, questioned the legal basis of the case and the DOJ's standing to bring it. Judge Mark Bennett, a Trump appointee, expressed confusion about the request, stating, 'How can we do that?' and noting that Congress and the California Legislature have already established that noncitizens cannot vote. The judge emphasized that the lawsuit appeared to challenge California's method of verifying voter eligibility rather than addressing a clear legal violation. item.title: Xbox and Netflix Negotiations for Gaming IP Adaptations Fall Apart Over Price Dispute
item.description: According to a report by Puck News' Matthew Belloni, Xbox and Netflix were in discussions for an exclusive multi-year deal to adapt several Xbox game franchises into TV shows and movies. The streaming giant reportedly offered $500 million for exclusive rights to develop projects based on Xbox's intellectual property over a seven-year period. However, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma allegedly demanded $800 million, leading Netflix to withdraw its offer. Microsoft stated they would not comment on specific bids but emphasized receiving 'record-breaking interest' in their IP, with a focus on finding the right creative partners and release models for each franchise. The failed negotiations have prompted Xbox to seek smaller, less exhaustive deals with multiple production partners, aiming to replicate the success of the Minecraft movie and Fallout TV series on Amazon. item.title: Texas Mother Who Consistently Voted for Trump Faces Cancer Treatment Costs and Financial Uncertainty
item.description:
Cindy Banda, a single mother from McAllen, Texas, is facing the financial and emotional challenges of breast cancer treatment while caring for six children. The Associated Press report follows Banda as she returns to a Houston cancer center, where she underwent surgery to remove her right breast a year earlier. Despite the operation and subsequent treatment, she remains uncertain whether the cancer has been eliminated from her body. Her doctors have indicated that overcoming the disease will be difficult.
Banda maintains an optimistic outlook, describing herself as a positive person. However, the financial pressures associated with cancer care have become a significant concern. As a single parent responsible for six children, she is determined to preserve her family's stability throughout her treatment. item.title: Geopolitical Expert Warns of Escalation Trap in Iran Conflict Post-Midterms
item.description: A geopolitical expert, Robert Pape, a political scientist at the University of Chicago, has warned that President Donald Trump is facing a significant strategic trap in the ongoing conflict with Iran. In a recent Substack essay, Pape outlined how Iran could leverage economic pressure to force the U.S. into a dangerous escalation cycle. The expert identified the two months following the November midterm elections as the 'most dangerous' period in the conflict, noting that the lame-duck Congress would have limited ability to constrain Trump's actions, especially if Democrats gain significant ground in the midterms. Pape argued that Iran's strategy involves creating economic strain through pressure on the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf oil supplies, forcing Washington to choose between making substantial concessions to Iran or escalating military actions. item.title: Former DOJ Attorney Warns of Pardon Limitations That May Affect Trump Administration Officials
item.description: A former Justice Department pardon attorney, Liz Oyer, has identified a legal loophole in presidential pardons that could have significant implications for officials in the Trump administration. Oyer, who served as Trump's pardon attorney until her dismissal by Attorney General Todd Blanche in 2025, argues that administration officials who believe they can avoid legal consequences through presidential pardons are making a critical error. She highlights the case of Philip Esformes, a businessman pardoned by Trump during his first term for a healthcare fraud scheme, where the Department of Justice pursued charges on six counts where the jury had not reached a verdict. Oyer explains that pardons typically cover only the specific charges for which a person was convicted, not all related allegations. item.title: Two Cyclists Killed in Montclair Collision with Drunk Driver During Pre-Halloween Ride
item.description: A tragic incident occurred in Montclair, California, when a vehicle struck multiple bicyclists during a pre-Halloween ride, resulting in two fatalities and several injuries. According to the Montclair Police Department, a group of approximately 30 cyclists was riding east on Kingsley Street around 10:39 p.m. on Saturday when a driver traveling in the opposite direction collided with several of them. One cyclist was pronounced dead at the scene, while another died later at a hospital. A third victim remained hospitalized in stable condition, and a fourth suffered a minor head laceration but declined further medical treatment. The driver fled the scene but was apprehended by police with the help of witnesses, who tracked him to his home near the collision site. Valentin Alberto Rodriguez, 38, was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence, causing injury or death, felony hit-and-run, and gross vehicular manslaughter. item.title: Gazze's Bread Line Stretches for Meters Amid Food Crisis
item.description: Gaza Strip continues to face a severe food crisis as bread lines stretch for meters outside bakeries. With insufficient flour supply, only seven bakeries remain operational across the region, while the rest face closure within days. Israel's ongoing attacks and blockade have reduced the amount of flour entering Gaza to below the required level. Current supplies only allow bakeries to operate for one day, forcing Gazans to wait hours in line to bring bread home. The Gaza Bakers Association reported that flour stocks in warehouses have been completely depleted, with only seven of the total 20 bakeries still functioning. Association President Abdel Nasser al-Ajrami stated that one thousand tons of flour entered Gaza today, with another thousand expected tomorrow. He emphasized that flour is not sold on the market and that current supplies only sustain bakeries for one day, stressing the need for uninterrupted supply. item.title: Knicks Send Employees Fake Championship Ring Offers in Phishing Test
item.description: The New York Knicks organization recently conducted a phishing test by sending employees a fake email offering championship rings, a common tactic used to assess employee awareness of phishing attempts. The email, which appeared to come from a legitimate source, contained a link that would have led to a fake website designed to capture login credentials. This type of test is intended to evaluate whether employees can recognize and avoid phishing scams, which are a major security threat in the workplace. However, the approach has been criticized for being ineffective and potentially counterproductive. Many employees, after receiving the email, questioned its legitimacy and reported it to IT, demonstrating that the training they had received was effective. The test, however, was poorly designed, as it did not include any elements that would have been recognizable to someone who had paid attention to anti-phishing training. item.title: Grok Unveils First Seven Minutes of AI-Generated 'Odyssey' Film
item.description: Grok, the AI model developed by Elon Musk's xAI, has released the first seven minutes of its AI-generated film adaptation of Homer's 'Odyssey.' This release comes three months after Musk announced plans for a full-length, 'historically accurate' movie version of the epic poem. The AI-generated footage, described as 'Episode 1 of our Odyssey series,' has been created in collaboration with Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker. The release follows Musk's criticism of Christopher Nolan's recent 'Odyssey' film, which he criticized for casting nonwhite and transgender actors. Nolan's version, which relied on practical filmmaking across six countries with a large cast and crew, became a box office success and is considered a leading contender for Academy Awards. In contrast, Grok's version features a British-accented narrator, characters with skin tones approved by Musk, and dialogue described as 'stilted' and lacking artistic merit. item.title: Smart City Surveillance in Africa Raises Concerns Over Privacy and Political Control
item.description: The article examines the growing use of smart city surveillance technologies across Africa, with a focus on Uganda, and highlights concerns about their potential for political control and privacy violations. The Ugandan government has implemented systems like the Automated Express Penalty System (EPSAuto), which uses CCTV cameras, automatic number plate recognition (ANPR), and intelligent transport monitoring systems (ITMS) to fine motorists. However, the system faced public backlash due to issues like duplicated fines and unclear speed limits, leading to its suspension. The article notes that Uganda's surveillance infrastructure, largely built with Chinese technology through companies like Huawei and ZTE, has expanded to cover major towns and municipalities. A report co-edited by the author, Wairagala Wakabi, reveals over $2 billion spent on surveillance in 11 African countries, with Chinese companies financing much of this infrastructure. item.title: Trump Faces Outrage Over Racist Remarks Targeting Progressive Senate Candidate
item.description: On October 25, 2026, former President Donald Trump sparked widespread condemnation during a campaign rally in Port Huron, Michigan, where he criticized Democratic Socialist Abdul El-Sayed, a Senate candidate, by accusing him of supporting jihadists. Trump stated, 'Anyone with that record of supporting jihadists would be screened and unable to get a seat on an airplane. They certainly should not give him a seat in the United States Senate,' and added, 'He would be the only Senator who is required to go through a metal detector before he's allowed to go into the Senate.' Trump's post, dated October 25, 2026, at 11:42 PM Eastern, labeled Obama as 'a grossly incompetent President' and accused him of paying Iran billions of dollars while enabling nuclear proliferation. Trump also criticized Obama's support for Democratic candidates, including Hillary Clinton and Kamala Harris, claiming they 'lost in all directions and ways.' The president then turned his attention to El-Sayed, a physician and epidemiologist who previously led Detroit's health department, accusing him of being a 'Fake Doctor' who runs 'the WORST CLINIC IN AMERICA' and a 'Muslim Brotherhood Jihadist' who 'hates Jews and Blacks and AMERICANS and TRUMP.' Trump offered no evidence for these claims. He also touted his own achievements in Michigan, stating he 'won Michigan

item.title: Tracy Grijalva Explains His Departure from Ronnie James Dio's Band
item.description: Tracy Grijalva, known as Tracy G, has shared his reasons for leaving Ronnie James Dio's band after six years. In a forthcoming interview with Guitar World, Grijalva explains that he was asked to switch from lead guitar to rhythm guitar, which he felt would diminish his creative expression. 'I played lead for Ronnie for six years, now he asked me to play rhythm. If you take solos from me, then I'm out,' he stated. Grijalva joined Dio's band in 1993, following two auditions, and contributed to the albums 'Strange Highways' (1993) and 'Angry Machines' (1996). He was replaced by Craig Goldy, who had previously played on Dio's 1987 album 'Dream Evil.' Grijalva clarified that he wasn't personally offended by the decision, noting that it was likely driven by management and label pressure rather than Dio's preference. He maintained that he and Dio remained on good terms, even calling him during Christmas after leaving to wish him a Merry Christmas, though he never received a response. Grijalva

item.title: White House Deputy Chief of Staff Warns Anonymous Leakers of Consequences
item.description: Dan Scavino, the White House Deputy Chief of Staff and a longtime aide to President Donald Trump, issued a stern warning to anonymous leakers within the administration late Saturday night. In a post on X, Scavino accused unnamed officials of leaking information to media outlets to 'angle for the next big job,' calling them 'pathetic, self-absorbed, egotistical losers' and stating that the administration 'knows who some of you disloyal, power-hungry cowards are.' He tagged Trump's personal account and official White House handles, emphasizing the message's gravity. The post, which Scavino pinned to his profile, garnered nearly 100,000 views within hours. This warning comes amid growing reports of internal conflict within Trump's administration, particularly as the 2026 midterm elections approach. item.title: U.S. Intelligence Warns of Advanced Iranian Plots Targeting Officials in Middle East
item.description: According to a memo from the Director of National Intelligence to the Secretary of State, Iranian efforts to target U.S. personnel in the Middle East have reached 'advanced stages.' The memo, which was confirmed as authentic by a U.S. official, states that the 'lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages.' The U.S. has been scaling back its troop presence and diplomatic personnel across the region, with the State Department ordering further reductions in staff at multiple diplomatic posts in Lebanon, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Jordan. These posts have already been operating under 'restricted operations' status with limited staffing since the start of the war. The memo also notes that the risk is 'relevant to more individuals than are currently cleared to receive this information,' and that efforts are being made to downgrade intelligence so it can be shared with State Department personnel. item.title: Trump Criticizes Senator Murkowski Over Alaska Senate Race Lawsuit
item.description: President Donald Trump has launched a series of attacks on Senator Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) through his Truth Social platform, accusing her of being the 'worst Republican senator' and suggesting she is complicit in a supposed Democratic plot to undermine the Alaska Senate race. The controversy stems from Murkowski's recent statement that the Trump administration's Justice Department should not have filed a lawsuit challenging Alaska's ranked-choice voting system in the Senate race between incumbent Dan Sullivan and his opponent, Mary Peltola. Trump's post, written near midnight on October 25, 2026, claims Murkowski only won her election due to 'corrupt ranked choice voting' and accuses her of opposing the DOJ lawsuit to allow Democrats to 'steal the election.' He attached an image of the Alaska Senate ballot showing two candidates with similar names—Dan S. Sullivan and Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.—to support his claim that the ballot was a 'total Democrat scam' meant to confuse voters. Trum

item.title: Historic Photo Shows Horse Performing 'Play Dead' Trick for 1900s Fairgoers
item.description: A vintage photograph from the early 1900s captures Del Womack, an animal trainer and regional performer, demonstrating a trained horse's 'play dead' trick for amused children. The image, dated circa 1900, shows the horse lying motionless on the ground while still hitched to a cart, with a black hat placed near its flank serving as the cue for the performance. Womack, who performed at local fairs and exhibitions, used this simple yet effective method to entertain audiences. The photograph reveals the lighthearted nature of the scene, with Womack and a smiling boy standing beside the cart, contrasting with the typical panic that would accompany a collapsed carriage horse. Such animal performances were popular entertainment at fairs during this era, showcasing the training skills of performers like Womack. The Missouri State Archives, which holds the photograph, provides historical context for this early 20th-century entertainment practice. The image offers a glimpse into the cultural pra

item.description: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMD) reported strong quarterly earnings on August 4th, surpassing analyst expectations with $1.66 earnings per share (EPS) compared to the consensus estimate of $1.62. The company's stock price has been volatile, with a two-week high of $658.52, and it has a market capitalization of $843.64 billion. item.title: Tesla Stock Faces Pressure Amid AI Buildout Delays and Market Sell-Off
item.description: Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) experienced a 0.6% decline in stock price, opening at $372.22 on Friday. The company reported quarterly earnings of $0.48 per share, slightly exceeding analyst estimates of $0.46. Revenue reached $28.05 billion, marginally below the consensus estimate of $28.06 billion. Despite the slight earnings beat, Tesla faces significant challenges including delays in its Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology deployment, incomplete AI infrastructure buildout (only 15% complete), and broader market pressures. The Nasdaq index sell-off, renewed skepticism about AI spending returns, higher oil prices, and geopolitical tensions have collectively pressured high-valuation technology stocks like Tesla. Analysts have mixed ratings on the stock, with one Strong Buy, twenty-four Buy, twenty Hold, and three Sell ratings. item.title: White House Communications Director Uses Offensive Slur in Social Media Post, Drawing Criticism
item.description: The White House communications director, Steven Cheung, has come under fire for using a highly offensive slur targeting individuals with Down syndrome in a social media post. The incident occurred after journalist Andrew Feinberg asked a follow-up question during a White House press briefing, which led to Cheung's tweet using the derogatory term. Cheung, a former UFC employee and Trump campaign staffer, has been criticized for his history of bullying and using inflammatory language, including terms like 'libturds' and 'Demo-rats.' The article highlights Cheung's background, noting his role in Trump's first presidency and his current position as communications director. It also discusses the broader context of declining political discourse under Trump's administration, with Cheung exemplifying the lowest point in White House communication standards. item.title: AI Labs' Strategy to Replace Engineers Backfires as Free Models Undermine Customer Base
item.description: The article examines a critical flaw in the business model of major AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic, which aimed to replace human software engineers with AI tools to capture the revenue streams of companies that traditionally paid for software development. The core idea was that by selling AI-powered engineering solutions to businesses, these labs could profit from the salaries companies would no longer need to pay their human employees. However, the strategy failed because the AI tools were made available to the public at very low costs—around $20 per month—enabling hobbyists and open-source developers to create free alternatives that undercut the very businesses the AI labs depended on for revenue. The article compares this situation to historical examples like the Spanish silver trade and De Beers' diamond monopoly, where making a valuable resource abundant led to its devaluation. item.title: Criminal Hackers Exploit AI Guardrails to Conduct Cyberattacks
item.description: According to a recent report by CrowdStrike, criminal hackers are effectively bypassing AI safety measures to conduct sophisticated cyberattacks using agentic AI. The threat intelligence firm analyzed attacks carried out between May and August by four different threat groups operating in Chinese, Spanish/English, Indonesian, and Russian. All groups successfully circumvented AI model safeguards, primarily by manipulating Anthropic's Claude and DeepSeek models to carry out unauthorized hacking activities. Researchers found that attackers used various techniques to bypass guardrails, including framing their activities as legitimate penetration testing, adding files to agent directories to show authorization, and employing traditional jailbreaking methods through carefully crafted prompts. The Chinese-speaking group demonstrated particularly sophisticated tactics, using a tool called ClawGod to modify Claude Code's system prompts to remove cybersecurity restrictions. item.title: Jeff Garlin Reveals Mental Health Struggles Following 'Goldbergs' Departure After HR Investigation
item.description: Jeff Garlin, the actor known for his role as Murray Goldberg on the ABC comedy series 'The Goldbergs,' has disclosed that he considered suicide following his departure from the show in December 2021. The decision to leave came after an HR investigation prompted by multiple complaints about his behavior on set. Garlin shared his experience on Ted Danson's podcast 'Where Everybody Knows Your Name,' revealing he reached out to his 'Curb Your Enthusiasm' co-star Susie Essman to inform her he planned to end his life. He stated, 'I had a nervous breakdown, and I was going to commit suicide.' Essman then contacted Garlin's ex-wife Marla, girlfriend Sari, and friend Brad Morris to help him seek treatment. Garlin checked into rehab in Cincinnati, Ohio, where he underwent dialectical behavior therapy (DBT), which helped him overcome his suicidal thoughts. item.title: Greece Implements Social Media Ban for Minors Under 15 Starting January 2027
item.description: Greece has passed legislation banning children under 15 from using social media platforms, effective January 1, 2027. The law requires social media platforms to implement reliable age verification systems and mandates that parents use government-backed applications to restrict access. Noncompliance with these requirements will be penalized under the EU's Digital Services Act. The legislation was introduced by Greece's digital governance and AI minister, Dimitris Papastergiou, who stated, 'It would have been very easy to do absolutely nothing today and wait for the perfect European law. But the challenge is here. Children are sinking into the internet every day, and I believe a responsible government must do what it is obliged to do.' The bill was passed by Prime Minister Mitsotakis' majority government, despite opposition from minority parties. Greece previously implemented a ban on mobile phones in schools in 2024, and public opinion polls indicate strong support for the new social me

item.title: Color Photos Capture Munich Oktoberfest's Post-War Revival in the 1950s
item.description: The article presents a collection of color photographs from the Munich Oktoberfest in the early 1950s, a period marking the festival's return after World War II. These images showcase the vibrant atmosphere of the Theresienwiese, featuring crowded beer tents, traditional Bavarian attire, lively crowds, and amusement rides. The photos document the festival's resurgence as a beloved German tradition during a time of postwar recovery and renewed celebration. Taken just a few years after the Oktoberfest fully resumed following the war, the photographs offer a nostalgic glimpse into the event's history more than seventy years ago. The article emphasizes the cultural significance of these images, preserving the spirit of the festival as it regained its place in German cultural life. The photographs provide a visual record of the festival's evolution and its importance as a symbol of community and tradition in postwar Germany. item.title: The Scots Who Ruled the Cocos Islands: A Forgotten Chapter in Colonial History
item.description: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands, a remote archipelago in the Indian Ocean, were once under the rule of a Scottish family, the Clunies-Rosses, who established a unique colonial administration that lasted for over a century. The Clunies-Ross family, originally from Scotland, arrived on the islands in the early 19th century and gradually took control of the territory, which was then known as the Cocos Islands. They established a plantation economy based on coconut production, which became the backbone of the local economy. The family's rule was characterized by a blend of Scottish governance and local customs, creating a distinct cultural identity on the islands. The Clunies-Rosses maintained their authority until the mid-20th century when the British government took over the administration of the islands. The legacy of the Scottish family remains evident in the architecture, place names, and cultural practices of the Cocos Islands. This historical period is a fascinating example of how a sma

item.title: Olivia Newton-John and Pat Carroll's Early Musical Partnership in 1960s London
item.description: Before Olivia Newton-John became a global pop icon and the star of Grease, she spent the mid-1960s performing as part of a pop vocal duo called 'Pat and Olivia' alongside her close friend and fellow Australian singer, Pat Carroll. The duo formed after both artists met in the Australian music circuit and appeared on local television shows like Swallow's Juniors. They moved to London in 1966, sharing a flat in Hampstead with Olivia's mother, and began performing together in nightclubs and pubs across the UK and Europe. Their repertoire included energetic pop covers and folk-blended harmonies, and they gained traction by backing major stars like Cliff Richard and securing television appearances. However, their partnership ended abruptly in 1966 due to UK immigration laws when Pat Carroll's visa expired, forcing her to return to Australia. item.title: Study Reveals Language's Safety Bias Challenges Long-Standing Scientific Model
item.description: A groundbreaking study from the University of Vermont challenges a 70-year-old scientific framework for understanding word meaning. Researchers analyzed billions of word uses across diverse texts and discovered that language meaning is organized around power, danger, and order rather than emotion alone. The traditional Valence-Arousal-Dominance (VAD) model, developed in the 1950s, has been widely used in psychology, linguistics, and AI to categorize emotional content. However, the new research introduces 'ousiometrics,' a mathematical approach that identifies three fundamental dimensions: power (weak vs. powerful), danger (safe vs. dangerous), and structure (ordered vs. chaotic). The study found that this new framework explains over 90% of word meaning variation, compared to 72% for the VAD model. Crucially, the research reveals a pervasive safety bias in language, where words associated with safety appear far more frequently than those related to danger. This finding reinterprets the

item.title: Trump Administration's DOJ Files Lawsuit to Block Alaska Senate Election Results Amid Confusion Over Name Similarity
item.description: The Trump administration's Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed a lawsuit seeking to prevent Alaska officials from certifying the results of the U.S. Senate race if Senator Dan Sullivan loses his reelection bid. The lawsuit claims that the presence of a namesake challenger, retired educator Dan J. Sullivan, on the ballot could mislead voters intending to support the incumbent. The case has drawn criticism from attorneys and lawmakers who argue it is legally unfounded and politically motivated. The lawsuit alleges that if votes intended for Senator Sullivan were instead cast for Dan J. Sullivan, the incumbent would have won under Alaska's ranked choice voting system. However, legal experts have dismissed the claim as frivolous, with one attorney stating it would receive a 'D-' from a first-year law student. item.title: Military Recruitement Rituals and a Tragic Death at College Football Game
item.description: On October 17, 2026, an airman died during a pregame ceremony at a UTSA vs. Navy football game in San Antonio. The airman, assigned to the 6th Combat Training Squadron, lost control while rappelling from the stadium rafters and hit the turf hard. He was later pronounced dead at a local hospital. The incident occurred during the university's annual Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans ceremony, which typically involves military personnel performing demonstrations. The Air Force has not released his name, and the death is under military investigation. The article explores the broader context of military recruitment through sports events, referencing a 2015 Senate report by John McCain and Jeff Flake that revealed the Pentagon spent $53 million on marketing and advertising contracts with sports teams between 2012 and 2015. item.title: CentreBC Leader Elenore Sturko Defeated in Surrey South Election
item.description: Elenore Sturko, leader of the CentreBC political party, has lost her bid to win back her former seat in Surrey South, according to projections from The Canadian Press decision desk. Sturko, a former RCMP officer, was previously elected to the riding in 2022 as a B.C. Liberal before joining the Conservatives in 2024 and winning in nearby Surrey-Cloverdale that year. However, she was ejected from the Conservative party by former leader John Rustad, who cited the need for caucus unity. Sturko then sat as an Independent before announcing in September that she was joining CentreBC, along with seven other Conservative defectors. All except Sturko returned to the Conservatives shortly after Kerry-Lynn Findlay resigned as leader and was replaced by interim leader Lorne Doerkson ahead of the provincial election. item.title: Sen. Baldwin Proposes Bill to Prevent Federal Agents from Intimidating Voters at Polling Locations
item.description: U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) has introduced the Safe Access to the Polls Act, a legislative measure designed to protect voters from potential intimidation or interference by federal agents at polling locations. The bill prohibits the use of federal funds to deploy U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), or National Guard personnel near polling places, establish checkpoints along routes to polling locations, or interfere with voters' access to their designated polling sites. This initiative comes amid heightened concerns over President Trump's repeated threats to send federal agents to polling places, with several of his appointees refusing to rule out such actions during public hearings or media appearances. Senator Baldwin criticized the President for prioritizing political interference over addressing critical issues such as rising gas and grocery costs, trade wars affecting farmers, and significant Medicaid cuts. item.title: Milwaukee Brewers Rally Past Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 to Take 2-0 World Series Lead
item.description:
The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 in Game 2 of the 2026 World Series on Saturday night at American Family Field, overcoming an early four-run deficit to take a commanding 2-0 lead in the best-of-seven championship series. Milwaukee's comeback continued its strong postseason form, as the team demonstrated its ability to recover from difficult starts and capitalize on crucial late-game opportunities.
The Rays took control immediately, scoring four runs in the top of the first inning against rookie pitcher Logan Henderson. Liam Hicks highlighted the early surge with a two-run home run, putting Tampa Bay in a strong position. However, the Brewers responded with two runs in the bottom half of the inning, reducing the deficit to 4-2.

item.title: Brewers Overcome Four-Run Deficit in Game 2 to Take 2-0 Series Lead Against Rays
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers staged a dramatic comeback in Game 2 of the World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays, overcoming a four-run deficit to secure a 5-4 victory. The game, played at American Family Field in Milwaukee, saw the Rays take an early lead with four runs in the first inning, including RBI singles from Chandler Simpson and Junior Caminero and a two-run home run by Liam Hicks. The Brewers chipped away at the deficit, with William Contreras and Garrett Mitchell each recording RBI singles in the bottom of the first. The Brewers bullpen held the Rays scoreless for the remainder of the game, with Aaron Ashby extending his postseason scoreless streak to 15.2 innings. The turning point came in the sixth inning when Sal Frelick hit a solo home run off Ian Seymour, erasing the deficit. Cooper Pratt followed with an RBI single in the seventh inning to give Milwaukee a 5-4 lead. item.title: Stock Ownership Reaches Historic High for U.S. Households, Surpassing Dot-Com Bubble Levels
item.description: According to the Federal Reserve's latest Financial Accounts data, stocks now make up 48.2% of Americans' financial assets in the second quarter of 2026, marking the highest share since records began in 1945. This surpasses the 38.7% reached during the dot-com bubble and the 41% seen after the 2021 meme-stock frenzy. Households hold approximately $74 trillion in stocks compared to about $20 trillion in bank deposits and money market funds, representing a record $3.65 in stocks for every dollar of cash. The report highlights significant wealth concentration, with the top 1% owning about half of all stocks and the top 10% owning 88%, while the bottom half owns only about 2%. The article notes that much of the increase stems from rising stock prices rather than new investments, and historical data suggests that when stocks constitute a large share of household assets, future returns tend to be lower. item.title: Melbourne Endures Unseasonable Cold and Rain as MotoGP Event Cancelled
item.description: Melbourne is experiencing an unusual spring cold snap, with below-average temperatures, heavy rainfall, and icy winds causing significant disruptions. The city recorded over 22mm of rain in 12 hours on Sunday, with some areas like Altona receiving up to 40mm in 24 hours. The severe weather led to the cancellation of the Australian MotoGP event at Phillip Island, marking the end of the race at the iconic circuit. Organizers canceled the event due to poor visibility, unsafe track conditions, and the grounding of the medical helicopter, which was unable to operate because of the weather. The cancellation affected multiple races, including the MotoGP warm-up session, Australian Superbikes Race 3, and Motor3 race. Health authorities issued warnings about potential thunderstorm asthma emergencies due to high pollen counts combined with strong winds and thunderstorms in East Gippsland. item.title: Starlink Service Restored for Ukrainian Military After Temporary Restrictions
item.description: SpaceX has reportedly lifted restrictions on the Ukrainian military's use of Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink, following a period of connectivity issues that affected drone operations. The Wall Street Journal noted that Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara confirmed Starshield is now functioning normally, though the military continues testing and has not received an explanation for the previous restrictions. During a 10-day disruption, Ukrainian drones experienced internet loss at speeds around 100 mph, causing loss of control and increased vulnerability. President Donald Trump reportedly contacted Elon Musk to request restoration of Starshield service, with Musk previously claiming Ukraine violated Starlink terms by using it for offensive drone strikes. Musk stated that turning off Starlink would cause an immediate collapse of the Ukrainian front line, though he clarified this was a factual statement, not a threat. item.title: Critical PHP vulnerabilities prompt global cybersecurity agencies to advise website shutdowns
item.description: Global cybersecurity agencies have issued urgent warnings to organizations about two critical remote-code-execution vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language powering a vast majority of websites. The National Security Agency (NSA) and Europe's cybersecurity agencies advised organizations to take vulnerable websites offline immediately if they couldn't apply the emergency patch. The vulnerabilities, identified as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each carry a critical severity score of 9.2 out of 10. PHP released emergency patches at 13:35 UTC on October 21, 2026, ahead of its normal schedule, with fixed versions including PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Many government websites across Europe, including Finland's state IT services, the Netherlands' National Cyber Security Centre, and France's prefecture websites, went offline as officials raced to apply the patch. item.title: Brazil’s Presidential Runoff Pits Lula Against Flávio Bolsonaro Amid a Rightward Political Shift
item.description:
Brazilian voters are heading to the polls on October 25, 2026, in a presidential runoff between incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The election has become a closely contested battle that could reshape Brazil’s domestic policies and international relationships. Lula, 80, entered the race as the favorite but was overtaken by Flávio’s unexpectedly strong first-round performance, in which Bolsonaro received 2.2 million more votes than the incumbent. Neither candidate secured an outright majority.
Crime, corruption, and the cost of living have emerged as central campaign issues. Flávio has promised tougher measures against criminal organizations, including designating major factions as terrorist groups and expanding prisons. item.title: Trump Administration Accused of Assembling Mechanisms to Undermine Democratic Processes
item.description: The article discusses a speech by Chris Hedges, published on ScheerPost, which warns that the Trump administration is developing mechanisms to discredit election results, intimidate voters, and justify federal intervention based on claims of election fraud. The speech argues that these actions are part of a broader effort to make the administration's hold on power permanent. The article notes that this indictment extends beyond Trump, pointing to decades of corporate domination, bipartisan betrayal of working people, and the weakening of democratic institutions as factors that have prepared the ground for authoritarian rule. The author emphasizes that defending democracy in the event of election subversion would require mass organizing, nationwide strikes, and sustained public resistance from citizens whose futures are at stake. item.title: Día de los Muertos Celebration Lights Up Downtown Los Angeles Park
item.description: Gloria Molina Grand Park in downtown Los Angeles transformed into a vibrant cultural hub for the 2026 Día de los Muertos celebration, running from October 24 through November 2, 2026. The free outdoor exhibition invites residents to honor departed loved ones and celebrate community connections through various activities and altars. The event features a sacred processional and blessings by Ohtli Yollotl, honoring Indigenous roots, alongside family-friendly activities such as face-painting, sugar skull workshops, and wellness offerings from community partners like the Children's Institute. Participants are encouraged to leave personal items at the community altar as part of the tradition. The celebration includes altars dedicated to notable figures such as former Los Angeles Supervisor Gloria Molina, artist Betye Saar, and former Los Angeles Department of Water and Power employees. item.title: Avengers: Doomsday Official Trailer 2 Released by IGN
item.description: The official second trailer for 'Avengers: Doomsday' has been released by IGN, providing a glimpse into the upcoming Marvel Studios film. The trailer reveals that the movie will bring together beloved heroes from three distinct universes, setting them on a deadly collision course against an existential threat unlike anything they've faced before. item.title: Ground-based air defense systems deployed around Mar-a-Lago following Secret Service request
item.description: NORAD and USNORTHCOM have deployed ground-based air defense assets in and around Mar-a-Lago, Florida, according to officials. The deployment was made at the request of the U.S. Secret Service and under NORAD and USNORTHCOM authorities. A spokesperson for the military commands stated that due to security considerations, they cannot provide specific tactics, techniques, or procedural details. They referred further inquiries to the U.S. Secret Service. This deployment comes after NORAD reported on October 6 that more than 60 aircraft had been intercepted near Mar-a-Lago since President Donald J. Trump's return to office. WPTV, the local news station, captured video of the new defense equipment at President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The news report emphasizes the security measures taken to protect the property, which is the residence of former President Donald Trump. item.title: Florida Dengue Outbreak Continues to Grow Following Emergency Declaration
item.description: The Washington Post reports that dengue cases in Florida have continued to rise since three counties declared a state of emergency over what officials described as a 'wildly unusual' dengue outbreak. According to the article, infections of the mosquito-borne disease have nearly doubled in the past month since the emergency declaration. Hillsborough County is identified as the epicenter of the outbreak. The article, written by Alex DeLuca, notes that the situation remains concerning as the number of cases continues to climb. The piece includes a photograph of an Aedes aegypti mosquito, the primary transmitter of dengue, provided by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The article also mentions that the outbreak has been described as 'wildly unusual' by officials, suggesting that the current situation is not typical for the region. item.title: Trump admits he'd withhold federal aid to Georgia if GOP candidate loses
item.description: President Donald Trump made a controversial statement during a campaign rally in Perry, Georgia, on October 24, 2026, suggesting he would refuse to provide federal assistance to the state if Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff wins re-election. Trump, who endorsed Republican candidates Mike Collins for Senate and Rick Jackson for governor, told the crowd that he would not respond to calls from Ossoff, whom he mockingly referred to as 'Pee Wee Herman.' 'Sir, Pee Wee Herman's on [the phone]'—' tell him I'm not in!'—'But he needs money for Georgia!'—'I don't give a damn what he wants!' Trump imitated an aide's conversation, then added, 'Probably I shouldn't say that because they'll say this is not appropriate, but no, it makes a big difference.' The statement comes as Ossoff, first elected in 2020, faces Collins in a pivotal Senate race on November 3 that could determine control of the chamber. item.title: Bacterial compounds from insect-killing microbes may inspire new antibiotic development
item.description: Researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Terrestrial Microbiology and the University of Marburg have discovered how certain bacteria produce compounds that kill insects, which could lead to new antibiotics. The study focused on GameXPeptides produced by Xenorhabdus and Photorhabdus bacteria that live symbiotically with nematodes. When nematodes infect insects, these bacteria release GameXPeptides that kill the insect hosts. The researchers reconstructed the evolutionary history of GxpS, the enzyme responsible for producing these peptides, identifying 49 different compounds including side products. They found that natural selection, genetic drift, and recombination events shape the diversity of these nonribosomal peptides, which belong to a class of compounds used in antibiotics like penicillin. The PHP Foundation reported no successful exploitation of these bugs so far, but millions of exploitation attempts were observed within hours of the vulnerabilities being publicly disclosed, according to Cloudflare analysis. Researchers from security companies like Calif, OpenAI, and Wiz independently discovered these flaws using AI tools, with some of the underlying issues first identified in 2024. item.title: MS NOW Host Interrupts Democratic Congressman Over Election Integrity Concerns
item.description: On October 24, 2026, during a segment on 'The Weekend' program, MS NOW host Jonathan Capehart interrupted Democratic Congressman Joe Morelle (D-N.Y.) regarding concerns about President Donald Trump's potential interference in the upcoming midterm elections. Capehart challenged Morelle's assertion that Congress holds the final authority over contested elections, arguing that Trump's actions, such as the construction at East Potomac Golf Links and the development of the East Wing area, demonstrate a pattern of presidential overreach. Morelle maintained that Trump has no role in election administration and would need to persuade numerous citizens to alter votes, which he deemed unlikely given the presence of bipartisan observers. He acknowledged a worst-case scenario involving military intervention but emphasized that the American people would resist such a coup. Capehart, however, expressed frustration, stating that Trump's disregard for judicial rulings and his personal vendetta against

item.title: Tea Preparation Methods Linked to Heart Health Benefits in Major Study
item.description: A recent study published in the New York Post highlights the significant impact of tea preparation methods on heart health. Researchers analyzed data from over 485,000 individuals aged 30 to 79, tracking their tea-drinking habits and cardiovascular health over a nine-year period. The findings revealed that habitual tea drinkers had a 12% lower risk of all vascular diseases compared to infrequent drinkers, with the lowest risk observed among those consuming six to eight cups daily. The study also found that black tea showed more consistent associations with lower health risks than green tea, due to differences in post-harvest processing. Black tea undergoes oxidation, while green tea is steamed or roasted. However, the researchers emphasized that both types can be part of a heart-healthy diet. The strength of the tea, determined by brew time, tea-to-water ratio, and water temperature, also played a role, with medium-strength tea showing better health outcomes than weaker or stronger bre

item.title: Former GOP Congressman George Santos Pledges Drag Performance if Ohio Democrats Win Key Races
item.description: Former U.S. Representative George Santos (R-NY), expelled from Congress in 2023 following an ethics investigation and later convicted of federal crimes, has made a public pledge to perform in drag and take a cold plunge if Democrats win both the governor and senatorial races in Ohio. Santos, who was sentenced to over seven years in prison for wire fraud and identity theft before being granted a presidential commutation by Donald Trump, made the promise on social media platform X (formerly Twitter) on October 24, 2026. The Ohio races, featuring Republican Vivek Ramaswamy against Democrat Amy Acton for governor and Republican Senator Jon Husted facing former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown for re-election, are among the most closely watched statewide contests in the country. Santos initially stated he would dress in drag and do a cold plunge if Ohio 'goes Blue' for both races, later agreeing to the terms if either race goes to Democrats. item.title: Far-right Trump ally criticizes administration's approach to Putin, claims higher number of Americans held in Russia
item.description: Laura Loomer, a far-right activist and one of Donald Trump's most loyal allies, has publicly clashed with the Trump administration over its diplomatic approach to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Loomer, who has previously feuded with administration officials, made a startling claim on social media regarding the number of Americans held hostage in Russia. She stated that 22 Americans are being held by Russia, contradicting the previously reported figure of eight. Loomer claimed this higher number was confirmed by an official involved in negotiations for the release of American hostages, though she did not name the official or provide evidence for her claim. She also criticized the administration's handling of relations with Russia, calling Putin 'the most barbaric' leader when compared to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Loomer questioned how many Americans Ukraine is holding hostage, stating she believed the number was zero. Her comments come amid heightened tensions between

item.title: Ramaswamy Campaign Modifies Attack Ad After Fact-Checking Reveals Inaccurate Claim About Rival's Childhood
item.description: Vivek Ramaswamy's campaign has quietly revised its political advertisement targeting Ohio Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton, removing a disputed claim about Acton's childhood. The original ad featured Donna Arthur, Acton's estranged mother, who alleged that Acton never lived in a tent during her childhood. However, court records and a 1982 police report contradict this claim, showing that Arthur's family did reside in a tent at a campground. FactCheck.org verified Acton's account, which includes documentation of her stepfather's residence at the campground. The ad also included allegations of abuse Acton experienced from ages 10 to 12, which she stated occurred while her birth mother failed to protect her. The campaign initially planned to spend $4 million on the ad, which sparked bipartisan criticism. Ohio Governor Mike DeWine urged Ramaswamy to withdraw the ad, while President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance defended it. The campaign switched to a 30-second versio

item.title: Legal Expert Links DOJ's Election Concerns to Record Early Voting Trends
item.description: Norm Eisen, a veteran Trump adversary and former House Judiciary Committee special counsel during Trump's first impeachment, has identified record early voting as the likely cause behind the Justice Department's recent legal actions surrounding the 2026 midterm elections. Eisen, who is currently preparing to challenge the DOJ's lawsuit in federal court in California, argues that the administration's 'freakout' in courts is directly tied to unprecedented early voting numbers. By Saturday morning, over 25 million Americans had already cast ballots, breaking national records. Early voting in Texas is running 74 percent ahead of 2022, while Kansas has more than doubled its early voting pace. Eisen notes that these figures indicate strong Democratic enthusiasm in key states. Eisen's legal team, working with the Campaign Legal Center, is representing LULAC and the NAACP in opposing a DOJ lawsuit that demanded Los Angeles County set aside ballots from over 20,000 voters during active voting.

item.title: Colts Open to Trading Any Player Ahead of NFL Deadline Amid Coaching Changes
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts, sitting at a 2-4 record following the firing of general manager Chris Ballard, are expected to become major sellers at the NFL trade deadline. According to Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, the team has received strong trade interest in key players like Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and no player is expected to be 'off-limits' in trade discussions. This represents a significant shift for the Colts, who could potentially be the biggest sellers in the NFL this November. The team's decision to sell will likely depend on their performance in the coming weeks; if they fall below 2-4 and win one or fewer games over the next three weeks before the November 10 deadline, a fire sale may occur. Players like Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, who are set to hit free agency, could be dealt now to avoid the compensatory pick game. Even star running back Jonathan Taylor, though considered the least likely to be moved, could be on the trading block. The Colts' management, led by o

item.title: James Carville Highlights Polling Discrepancy as Potential Threat to Trump's Republican Party
item.description: Veteran Democratic political strategist James Carville recently discussed a critical polling metric during a podcast appearance that he believes could significantly impact the Republican Party's prospects in upcoming elections. In his Saturday episode of 'Politics War Room,' Carville emphasized the ratio of voters who strongly disapprove of President Donald Trump compared to those who strongly approve, noting the current split stands at approximately 50 percent disapproval versus 15 percent approval. He argued this metric is crucial for understanding voter turnout dynamics. Carville's guest, former Clinton White House political director Doug Sosnik, provided additional context in a strategy memo, stating that 52 percent of Americans hold a strong negative view of Trump's performance while only 12 percent strongly support him. Carville further highlighted the stark partisan divide, noting that 93 percent of Democrats disapprove of Trump while 80 percent of Republicans approve. Using a r

item.title: Netflix Stock Drops 51% After Advertising Revenue Forecast Cut
item.description: Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX), the world's largest streaming platform with over 325 million paying subscribers, has experienced a significant stock decline of 51% from its record high following a disappointing third-quarter earnings report. The company reported $12.9 billion in revenue for the third quarter of 2026, marking an 11.8% year-over-year increase, which matched analyst expectations but represented the slowest growth rate in three years. Investors reacted negatively, sending the stock down 6% in after-hours trading after the results were released on Wednesday, compounding a year-long decline for shareholders. The primary concern highlighted in the report was a downward revision to Netflix's advertising revenue forecast. Initially projected to double in 2026 to $3 billion, building on the $1.5 billion generated in 2025, the company revised this forecast to $2.7 billion due to slower-than-expected rollout of certain advertising capabilities. item.title: Trump dismisses GOP House loss predictions despite low approval ratings
item.description: Conservative columnist Byron York confronted President Donald Trump on Air Force One about the likelihood of Republicans losing the House in upcoming elections. During a conversation en route to a Sioux City, Iowa rally, York directly asked Trump if he believed the GOP would lose control of the House despite the enthusiasm at Trump's rallies. Trump responded by questioning York's perspective, stating, 'I just don't see it. There's such enthusiasm. You'll see, you'll go there today.' When pressed about his low approval rating of 38.8% according to RealClearPolitics, Trump dismissed it as 'fake,' claiming he believed his approval rating was much higher, possibly around 60%. York challenged Trump's perception of his base, noting that while Trump's rallies draw large, enthusiastic crowds, the broader electorate may not share the same sentiment. Trump insisted his base represented nearly 100% of the Republican Party, dismissing the influence of figures like the Bush family. He also maintain

item.title: Ramaswamy Campaign Faces Scrutiny Over Ad Featuring Accusations of Child Abuse
item.description: Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy's campaign is facing increased scrutiny after his running mate, Ohio state Senator Rob McColley, admitted that the campaign believes Democratic gubernatorial nominee Amy Acton was abused as a child by her stepfather. The controversy centers around a campaign ad featuring Acton's estranged mother, Donna Arthur, who calls her daughter a liar and urges Ohio voters not to support her. McColley clarified that the campaign does not dispute Acton's account of childhood abuse but instead accuses her of lying about the abuse in her adult political career. Court records confirm Acton's claims that her stepfather, Cledith Arthur, was arrested for raping her when she was 12, and her mother stayed with him until his death in 2004. The ad has drawn criticism from Democratic strategist Justin Barasky, who called it 'truly horrifying' that the campaign used the mother who stayed with the alleged abuser. CNN political reporter Aaron Blake noted the cam

item.title: Sen. Lisa Murkowski Criticizes Trump-Backed DOJ Lawsuit Over Alaska Senate Race
item.description: Senator Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) has garnered attention for publicly rebuking the Trump administration's Justice Department over a lawsuit concerning Alaska's Senate race. In a post on X, Murkowski stated that Alaskans do not require assistance in voting for their preferred candidates and that the State of Alaska has already clearly distinguished the candidates on the ballot. The Department of Justice, under Trump's direction, filed a lawsuit seeking to block certification of the race if Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan loses to Democrat Mary Peltola. The DOJ argued that voters might confuse Senator Sullivan with another candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan, who appears on the ballot without a party label. However, Alaska's ranked-choice voting system, which allows voters to rank multiple candidates, makes confusion unlikely. Murkowski's criticism of the lawsuit has been widely praised, particularly by Democrats and political analysts. Amy McGrath, a Democratic Senate candidate from Kentu

item.title: Serbia's newly elected parliament features a majority of academics and professionals
item.description: Serbia has elected a parliament with a significant number of academics and professionals, marking a shift from the previous 13 years of populist authoritarian rule under Aleksandar Vučić. The Student List – Students Are Winning movement, which emerged from student protests following a train station collapse in November 2024, secured 141 seats in the 250-member National Assembly. Over half of the elected representatives hold a Ph.D. or M.D., including astrophysicists, engineers, chemists, and medical researchers. The new parliament aims to combat corruption, establish meritocracy, and restore academic freedom, which had been eroded under Vučić's government. Universities had become politicized, with critics sidelined and funding distributed based on political connections rather than merit. The Student List promises more academic autonomy, stable science funding, and affordable education to address the brain drain. University rector Vladan Đokić and bioarchaeologist Sofija Stefanović high

item.title: El calendario romano: cómo un plebeyo democratizó el uso del tiempo
item.description: La noticia explora la historia del calendario romano, centrándose en la figura de Rómulo, el mítico primer rey de Roma, quien fundó la ciudad en el año 753 a.C. y creó un calendario inicial de 10 meses con 304 días, conocido como 'a.u.c.' (ab urbe condita). Este calendario, que comenzó con meses nombrados en honor a dioses y conceptos como Martius (marzo), Aprilis (abril), Maius (mayo) e Iunius (junio), carecía de los meses restantes, que se designaron simplemente con números romanos. El sistema resultó inadecuado para la agricultura debido a su desfase con las estaciones, lo que llevó al rey Numa a añadir dos meses en el 700 a.C.: Ianuarius (enero) y Februarius (febrero). Durante siglos, el calendario romano fue un instrumento político controlado por sacerdotes y aristócratas, quien lo mantenían como un secreto celosamente guardado. Esto generó una gran insatisfacción entre los ciudadanos, especialmente entre los plebeyos. En el 304 a.C., Cneo Flavio, un plebeyo que ocupaba el cargo d

item.title: Okdiario paga 242.000 euros a abogada de Koldo García en contexto de investigación judicial
item.description: El director de elDiario.es, Ignacio Escolar, ha publicado un boletín en el que analiza el pago realizado por la empresa editora de Okdiario, Dos Mil Palabras SL, de 242.000 euros a la abogada Leticia de la Hoz, defensora de Koldo García, imputado en un caso de corrupción. El pago se realizó el 27 de noviembre de 2025, el mismo día en que Eduardo Inda publicó una entrevista con García y este entró en prisión. La empresa de Okdiario justificó el pago como 'realización de un libro y una docuserie', pero fuentes cercanas a García aseguran que el contrato presentado es un borrador no firmado que establecía pagos superiores. Escolar señala que el pago es desproporcionado para un medio como Okdiario y cuestiona si está relacionado con las acusaciones de García de que alguien intentó interferir en su causa judicial. La Fiscalía Anticorrupción sospechaba que el PSOE había financiado la defensa de García, pero la abogada negó esta posibilidad. El juez Santiago Pedraz investiga si desde el PSOE s

item.title: Israel: El bloqueo político tras las elecciones y la influencia de los partidos árabes
item.description: Tras las elecciones israelíes, el panorama político sigue sin definirse, ya que ni la coalición de Benjamín Netanyahu ni el bloque opositor liderado por Gadi Eisenkot alcanzan los 61 escaños necesarios para formar gobierno en la Knéset. Los partidos árabes, con entre 17 y 18 diputados, podrían ser decisivos para desbloquear la situación. Eisenkot, en su discurso electoral, pidió construir una 'mayoría sionista', evitando explicitar si aceptaría el apoyo de los partidos árabes, lo que ha sido criticado por considerar que excluye su participación en el gobierno. Los partidos árabes, como la Lista Conjunta y Ra'am, han iniciado contactos para ofrecer apoyo a cambio de avances en la creación de un Estado palestino y medidas contra el crimen organizado. El diario Ynetnews presenta cinco escenarios para resolver el bloqueo, incluyendo la formación de un gobierno de unidad, la repetición de elecciones o un gobierno respaldado por los partidos árabes. La situación también interesa a Washington

item.title: El deshielo revela artefactos arqueológicos y rutas históricas en el contexto del cambio climático
item.description: La noticia aborda cómo el derretimiento de los hielos, acelerado por el cambio climático, está exponiendo artefactos arqueológicos de gran importancia histórica. El descubrimiento del Hombre de Hielo (Ötzi) en 1991, un cuerpo prehistórico conservado en el hielo durante 5.300 años, permite entender la vida cotidiana de la Edad del Cobre. Los análisis de Ötzi han revelado detalles sobre su dieta, tatuajes, genética y enfermedades, como la presencia de Helicobacter pylori. Además, el deshielo ha expuesto otros hallazgos, como un bosque de pinos de más de 5.000 años en las Montañas Rocosas y una antigua ruta vikinga en Noruega con objetos como ropa, herramientas y estiércol de caballos. Los arqueólogos destacan que estos descubrimientos son frágiles y que, una vez expuestos, pueden desaparecer rápidamente. El estudio de 2025 muestra que los glaciares perdieron alrededor de 270 mil millones de toneladas de hielo anuales entre 2000 y 2023. Los investigadores enfatizan la urgencia de rescatar

item.title: Fiscalía y juez cambian posición tras revelar pagos de Okdiario por defensa de Koldo García
item.description: La abogada Leticia de la Hoz, imputada en el caso Leire Díez, ha denunciado que la Fiscalía Anticorrupción y el juez Santiago Pedraz han ignorado durante meses los pagos realizados por la editorial Dos Mil Palabras, S.L. (propiedad de Okdiario) para financiar su defensa en el caso relacionado con Koldo García. Según la información proporcionada, la empresa editora de Okdiario, cuyo fundador es Eduardo Inda, pagó dos facturas por un total de 242.000 euros a la abogada, correspondientes a los meses de noviembre de 2025 y enero de 2026. La abogada, que había negado públicamente que el PSOE hubiera financiado su defensa, solicitó al juez que la liberara de su secreto profesional para revelar quién había pagado los honorarios. Sin embargo, la Fiscalía Anticorrupción inicialmente se negó a investigar estos pagos, hasta que cambió de criterio y el juez también modificó su posición, pidiendo las facturas que finalmente fueron presentadas el pasado jueves.
